notes.summary: feat: simplify WSC11 setup - fixed 9600 baud, broadcast id reset, Master/Slave
notes.body:
Four changes to the Thies WSC11 integration, plus one channel removal.

Fixed link settings. WSC11_BAUD (9600 8N1) replaces the configurable
wsc11.baud and the web UI's dropdown. 9600 8N1 is the factory default,
Thies allocates a separate order number to any Somfy variant shipping
otherwise (4.9056.10.801 = 19200), the unit sold in this range has no
such row and was bench-confirmed at exactly these settings, and this
firmware never writes BR or CI - so a station handed back to animeo
Suite still carries the baud it left the factory with and there is
nothing for an installer to match. No animeo Suite evidence exists on
the maintainer's machine; the reasoning is recorded in the doc so it is
not re-searched. An older /rs485.json carrying "baud" is ignored, not
migrated.

Dropped the -WIND2 (mean wind speed) channel: 8 per station, not 9.
Every wind gate here has to react to a gust, so an average is the wrong
input, and it only added two more points per station for a BMS
integrator to wire. The block read is unchanged (still the
hardware-confirmed FC 0x04 @35001 x 60). The RAM saving is small and
should not be oversold - RS485_MAX_SENSORS (23) and MAX_ACCUMULATORS
(44) are fixed-size arrays that do not shrink. All five hand-synced
RS485 tables renumbered: BACnet 71-86, KNX sub-offsets 23-38, the
Modbus block 23 -> 39 registers (1201-1239, still clear of the 1301
diagnostics base). Confirmed identical in order and length
programmatically afterwards.

"Reset unit id to factory" is now a Modbus broadcast to slave-address 0,
which the manual supports outright ("The weather station WSC11 supports
a write access for the slave-address 0"). It takes no "which station"
prompt - a broadcast addresses none in particular, which is the point
when handing stations back to animeo Suite. Its verification probe
failing is deliberately NOT an error: once several stations share id 1
they answer simultaneously and every reply fails CRC, which is exactly
what success looks like. buildWsc11WriteU32Request() now accepts unit id
0, widening WHO is written to and never WHAT - KY and ID remain the only
writable registers.

Master/Slave now applies to a WSC11 bus. Modbus RTU permits exactly one
master per bus, so several BuCo gateways sharing one WSC11 line must
have all but one set to Slave or they collide - stricter than the
SensorBus case, where the same checkbox is a recommendation. A Slave
runs listenPassiveWsc11(), which cannot reuse listenPassive(): that
one's buffer is 25 bytes against a 125-byte reply, and it delimits
frames by an inter-byte gap, which fails on Modbus because the foreign
master's request and the reply arrive as one blob after a
few-millisecond turnaround. It scans a rolling buffer for a CRC-valid
frame instead. armWsc11Job() refuses every job in Slave mode.

UI: all addressing controls moved into one <details> that opens itself
when count >= 2, in Slave mode, or when a station uses an id other than
1 - so the common case (one station, Master, factory id) shows only
"Number of stations", without making the shared-bus case unreachable.
Scan results are now a picker that fills a station slot on click. A
duplicate unit id is refused rather than merely warned about, which the
docs already (wrongly) claimed.

Also recorded, because it will be asked again: the WSC11 has no magnet,
reed contact or programming button. Modbus has no equivalent of KNX
physical-address programming, so singling out one of several stations
sharing an address is impossible in principle. An LED "identify" helper
via LC was considered and rejected - it widens the write allowlist and
LC lives in EEPROM.

Verified off-hardware: a host-compiled harness against the real
wsc11_protocol.cpp passes 21/21 - both of the manual's golden CRC
vectors, broadcast frames build, BR/CI/out-of-range still refused. Note
the manual prints CRC bytes in wire order under "low-Byte / high-Byte"
labels, so "CRC 4F7C" means 4F goes out first. Cost of the whole pass:
RAM +64 B, flash +592 B - the new listener outweighs the removed
channel. i18n complete in all six languages; help page extended.

Still unexercised on hardware: scan / assign / broadcast reset, and
Slave-mode listening. docs/wsc11-weather-station.md carries a
step-by-step first run for the broadcast.

notes.summary: feat: integrate the Thies WSC11 weather station (4.9056.11.001)
notes.body:
Reading confirmed on real hardware 2026-09-01, first attempt.

The WSC11 is an Adolf Thies GmbH product Somfy rebrands in the animeo range.
It is a plain Modbus RTU slave (9600 8N1, factory unit id 1) and speaks none of
this project's other RS485 protocols - see docs/wsc11-weather-station.md.

Added as another PRODUCT on the existing SOMFY_SENSORS port role, deliberately
NOT as a fifth Rs485PortRole. Reading it does need a Modbus RTU master - the
opposite direction from modbus_manager.cpp's server gateway - but a new port
role is exactly where the stability risk would have been: the ESP32-S3 has two
free UARTs already contested by the motor bus, the SensorBus and the Modbus
server, and a fifth role would have introduced a 3-roles-on-2-ports combination
that today's design makes unrepresentable by construction. So: no new
Rs485PortRole, no new UART, no new FreeRTOS task, no new stack, and nothing at
all when the product is not selected. What was added is one fixed read
transaction plus a bounded two-register write, never a general master stack.

Unavoidable consequence, enforced in rebuildSnapshot() as well as in the web
UI: a WSC11 and any Somfy SensorBus device cannot coexist, Inside Sensor Boxes
included - one UART carries one framing, and these are 8N1 vs 8E1.

The decoder normalizes every channel into the unit the matching Somfy key
suffix already carries (Lux, m/s, degrees, C, 0/1). That is load-bearing: the
web UI's formatters and all four gateway binding tables dispatch on the key
suffix, so this needed zero formatter/unit/scale changes anywhere - only new
table rows.

9 channels per station, up to 2 stations (WSC1-/WSC2-): brightness
north/east/south/west, wind speed and its mean, wind direction, outside
temperature, precipitation. RS485_MAX_SENSORS (23) and MAX_ACCUMULATORS (44)
deliberately did not move - they bound concurrently enabled keys, which the
mutual exclusivity above caps at max(23 Somfy, 18 WSC11).

18 appended rows in each of the five hand-synced RS485 tables: BACnet instances
71-88, KNX sub-offsets 23-40, the Modbus block 23 -> 41 registers, plus
gateway-setting.js's KG_RS485_MAP which serves both CSV exports. Confirmed
programmatically that all five agree in order and length.

Unit-id commissioning, because every station ships as id 1 and a multi-drop bus
needs distinct addresses. Modbus has no serial-number addressing and address 0
is a reply-less broadcast, so two stations both at id 1 cannot be told apart -
assignment is only possible with one station connected at a time. What the
firmware guarantees instead is that the installer never picks a number and a
duplicate can never be saved. Three installer-triggered jobs on SensorBusTask:
scan the bus, assign the id a station slot needs (verified by read-back at the
new id, since the manual leaves the write's own echo ambiguous), and reset to
factory id 1 so a station can be reused with animeo Suite. ID is holding
register 40003 and needs KY=234 first; the write path is bounded to those two
registers inside buildWsc11WriteU32Request() itself, not merely in the UI.

"Time from sensor" becomes real for this station, gated on the GPS-validity
bits of its own status word - without a fix it still reports a
plausible-looking timestamp computed from nothing. timegm() does not exist in
newlib on the ESP32, so the conversion uses an explicit daysFromCivil().

Cost, measured before/after on the same tree: RAM +1400 B, flash +9.7 KB.

Verified: the manual's two golden CRC vectors reproduced byte for byte, the
decoder cross-checked (including negative temperature, bit flips and truncated
frames), daysFromCivil() against calendar.timegm on 7 boundary dates, the five
gateway tables, no new i18n gaps, and the demo still builds.

Not yet exercised on hardware: the unit-id commissioning actions - the only
paths that write to the station - and time-from-sensor, which needs a GPS fix.

notes.summary: feat: identify the animeo WSC11 weather station and add an RS485 bring-up probe
notes.body:
A new "animeo Suite" sensor on COM5 turned out to be a WEATHER STATION COMPACT
WSC11 (order no. 4.9056.11.001) - an Adolf Thies GmbH product Somfy rebrands.
It does NOT speak Somfy SensorBus: no SB::Cmd, no CRC-8 poly 0xA5, no
`03 0F 5F` poll, and docs/sensorbus-protocol.md does not apply to it at all.
Chasing a "different poll command" inside SensorBus could never have worked;
the manufacturer's own manual is what settled it and enumerated the whole
search space.

Confirmed on hardware: Modbus RTU, 9600 8N1, slave id 1 - every setting at its
factory default, contact on the first active probe. Readings decoded and
cross-checked against physics (relative humidity, absolute humidity and dew
point mutually consistent at 26.6 C), so the register map and word order are
established rather than guessed.

scripts/wsc11_probe.py (+ .cmd, the usual Windows argument-dropping guard) is
the bring-up tool: passive listen, then a Modbus RTU and a THIES ASCII sweep
across all eight baud rates with optional id scans, and a wiring checklist when
nothing answers. It reuses modbus_crc16() and the inter-byte/response
two-timeout rule from scripts/modbus_selftest.py. Read-only by construction -
there is no write path in the file, because a blind write to the station's
CI/BR would move it to settings that then have to be searched for from scratch.

docs/wsc11-weather-station.md carries the register map and the traps worth
remembering: register addresses go on the wire literally (input register 30001
is 0x7531, no 30001/40001 offset subtraction), values are 32-bit high word
first, all 30 mirror into a single FC 0x04 @35001 x 60 poll, and passive
listening finds nothing because the station's automatic output defaults to off.

Not integrated into the firmware - that needs a Modbus RTU master role, the
opposite direction from this project's existing server/slave gateway.

Also carries the previously uncommitted CLAUDE.md section from the DALI Gateway
investigation; both are documentation-only additions to the same file.

notes.summary: fix: widen the Log chart hour view to a 2h window
notes.body:
The `hour` granularity spanned 3600s at 5 points, so the window was barely
wider than the 900s sampling step and a single sensor reading dominated it.
7200s at 9 points keeps the same 900s step (and the odd point count that puts
a real sample at the window centre) while showing enough context to read a
trend.

notes.summary: i18n: translate Reset to Auto, Switch Config, Test Bus Wires, Heartbeat into cs/de/fr/hr/pl
notes.body:
Finishes the batch started in the previous commit - these four were the only
names left deliberately English. Reset to Auto, Test Bus Wires and Heartbeat
translated straightforwardly (Heartbeat as each language's "sign of life"
idiom, matching the periodic keep-alive/watchdog telegram it names, not a
literal cardiac-pulse translation).

Switch Config needed a second pass the same day: the first translation used
each language's word for "switch" (toggle switch), copied uncritically from
Touch BuCo's own naming - user feedback that this is wrong, since the
animeo IB+ feature it names remaps physical push-buttons, not toggle
switches. Re-translated to each language's "button" word instead (Taster vs
Schalter in German, tipkalo vs prekidaÄŤ in Croatian, etc.), scoped narrowly
to this feature's own keys so the unrelated, correct existing use of
"switch" elsewhere (the generic UI toggle control, DIO hardware dry-contact
switches) is untouched.

Also fixes collateral damage from the previous commit's blind substring
replace: a few French/Croatian/Polish sentences had ended up with a
duplicated "configuration Configuration..." artifact (an English
cross-reference sitting unmerged next to its own translation) and one German
sentence kept an untranslated hyphenated compound ("Switch-Config-Einstellung")
that a plain space-separated match couldn't catch. Rewritten as clean
sentences rather than further substring patching, plus one Croatian
grammar-agreement fix.

notes.summary: i18n: translate remaining deliberately-English feature names into cs/de/fr/hr/pl
notes.body:
Frost/Ice, Lock Timer, Block Heat, Solar Heating, Maintain Heat, Event, Log,
ADIO/DIO/RS485 Configuration + RS485 Ports, Standard Position, My Position and
Run/Tilt Times were the only sidebar/breadcrumb feature names still shown in
English across every translated language - user feedback that this reads as
a translation bug, not a deliberate choice. Reused existing contextual
translations where one already existed elsewhere in the same file (e.g. Lock
Timer already had a per-language rendering inside the KNX heartbeat note) so
no feature ends up with two competing translations. MoCo ID/MoCo Settings and
the bare ADIO/DIO/RS485 abbreviations stay untranslated (nothing to
translate - MoCo is a Somfy-specific abbreviation, ID is the same loanword in
all 5 languages); Reset to Auto, Switch Config, Test Bus Wires and Heartbeat
stay English by explicit user choice. CLAUDE.md updated to describe the new
scope instead of claiming a blanket English-names policy.

Also fixes a real boot-time save race: the welcomeSeen and disclaimer-
acceptance container saves are fire-and-forget chains outside the
markConfigDirty()/__dirtyScopes tracking, so ensureNoPendingSavesBeforeRestart()
(used by RS485 Ports/Network Config/Gateway Setting before their own
ESP.restart()) couldn't see one still in flight - confirmed on real hardware
to restart the device mid-save and make the Welcome Screen reappear on every
later boot. window.__criticalFlagSavePromise now tracks both saves so that
guard can await them too.

and help.json (44 keys, English source already existed), then migrates every

notes.summary: feat: shared gateway diagnostics point set, exposed by all four gateways
notes.body:
New src/gateway_diagnostics.h/.cpp: one gateway-agnostic set of 11 points
describing the GATEWAY ITSELF rather than the installation, re-addressed by
each gateway in its own idiom. Until now every gateway published process data
and nothing about the device serving it, so a BMS could only tell "answers"
from "does not answer".

Points: firmware major/minor/patch, uptime (32-bit seconds), a liveness
counter, the worst loop() stall since boot, free heap, largest free block,
zone count, Ethernet up, RS485 comm-error summary.

Uptime and the liveness counter are a deliberate pair: uptime accumulates from
millis() (a hardware timer that runs even when no task is scheduled), the
liveness counter is incremented FROM loop(). Their divergence is the signal -
it reports the documented vendor EQSP32_SystemMa stall, which Modbus RTU
otherwise answers straight through from its own FreeRTOS task.

Per-gateway addressing:
  Modbus  - fifth register block, modbusDiagBase (1301), 16 registers.
            Two documented deviations: scale 1 (counters, not x10) and
            UNSIGNED (offsets 3-6 exceed 32767, so 0x8000 is not a sentinel
            inside this block).
  BACnet  - AI 60-68 / BI 69-70, created unconditionally, refreshed above the
            getHardwareStatusSnapshot() early return. Also fills in
            Device_Set_Time_Of_Restart().
  KNX     - base GA pair knxDiagBaseMain/Middle (5/0), sub-offset = point
            index. Needed two new encoders, knxEncodeDpt7()/knxEncodeDpt12():
            DPT 9 cannot represent a counter near 65535 to better than ~5, so
            a liveness counter published as DPT 9 would appear to stall - the
            exact fault it exists to detect.
  HA      - sensor/binary_sensor with entity_category "diagnostic" (first use
            in this codebase), own discovery builders so a monotonic counter
            gets state_class total_increasing rather than "measurement".

Also closes the Home Assistant availability/LWT gap, previously a listed open
question: retained "offline" Will in CONNECT, retained "online" after CONNACK,
availability_topic on every discovery payload. Nothing on the device can
report its own sudden death, so a diagnostic uptime entity does not substitute
for this.

Two bugs found while sizing that change, both pre-existing in origin:
  - publishCoverDiscovery()'s payload is 635 + 9*strlen(nodeId) bytes and
    overflowed from a 15-character Node ID (842 at the 23-char maximum). The
    pre-availability version was 541 + 8L and already overflowed at exactly 23
    - only the 11-char MAC-derived default kept real installs under it. Fixed
    by computing the worst case rather than eyeballing: MQTT_PUBLISH_PAYLOAD_MAX
    768 -> 1024, moved into mqtt_client.h so ha_manager.cpp references it
    instead of hand-copying the number, queue 16 -> 12 slots to hold the same
    heap budget. Both constants had to move together.
  - n += snprintf(...) accumulation in four builders: snprintf returns what it
    WOULD have written, so one truncation puts json + n out of bounds and
    underflows sizeof(json) - n. Clamped via jsonAdvance().

anyRs485SensorInCommError() added to sensorbus_manager rather than copying the
key list into gateway_diagnostics - the first version cost 460 bytes of
permanently resident .bss on every device, gateway enabled or not.

Cost: RAM +344 B, flash +5.0 KB (measured before/after). BACnet additionally
~1.2-1.5 KB heap while active, since AI/BI come from stock ai.c/bi.c.

Verified by execution, not inspection: both JS exports produce byte-exact the
same addresses as the firmware, the DPT encoders match hand-computed
big-endian values, the 11-point order is identical across all four firmware
tables and the selftest. scripts/modbus_selftest.py gains --diag-base and a
diagnostics sweep.

NOT yet verified on hardware: BACnet objects in BDT (and the heap figure at 32
zones), KNX in ETS (still no router), and the HA LWT power-cut test.

notes.summary: feat: Modbus gateway (TCP + RTU), confirmed end to end on real hardware
notes.body:
The fourth mutually exclusive gateway alongside BACnet/IP, KNX/IP and Home
Assistant MQTT, exposing the identical point set as 16-bit registers.

Two transports over one shared PDU layer, installer-selected:
  * Modbus TCP - Ethernet, port 502, serviced from loop()
  * Modbus RTU - one RS485 port, own ModbusRtu FreeRTOS task
Deliberately both, not RTU alone as first assumed: the ESP32-S3 has only two
free UARTs and a typical install already spends both, so RTU costs the
customer either the SensorBus or a motor bus. TCP costs no RS485 port.

No point table, no value cache, no publish sweep. The other three gateways
are push protocols and must cache values to detect change-of-value; Modbus is
pull, so reads resolve arithmetically straight from the existing
spinlock-guarded RAM snapshots. Measured static RAM with the gateway
disabled: 98 bytes. Data is also fresher than the other three - no sweep
staleness. The register map is dense on purpose: Modbus addresses are numeric
and unnamed, so a BMS must be able to write a fixed poll configuration that
does not shift when the installer enables another function.

Real-hardware verification (both transports, 23/23 including the full
exception matrix and physical product movement):
  * TCP over Ethernet
  * RTU on port 1 (TxD/RxD) bound to Serial2 while the motor bus held
    Serial1, 19200 8E1, unit id 1. ModbusRtu stack headroom ~3240 B free.
CRC-16 checked against three published Modbus reference vectors; the
client-side register-map CSV export checked to produce byte-exact agreement
with the firmware's own arithmetic.

One real firmware bug caught during bring-up: an FC16 {position, tilt} write
emitted TWO telegrams microseconds apart, the first carrying a stale tilt -
pushing to the IB+ queue wakes the equal-priority IbPlusTx task, which could
transmit before the second register was applied. Queue coalescing alone was
not a fix (it would have dropped the position instead). Resolved by deferring
the send to a new end-of-request hook, so at most one goto-position telegram
per zone per request.

Also adds scripts/modbus_selftest.py (raw sockets for TCP, pyserial only for
RTU) plus a .cmd wrapper, and docs/modbus-gateway.md.

notes.summary: fix: MoCo position auto-refresh no longer requires a gateway to be active

currentPosition/currentTiltAngle feed more than just BACnet/KNX/Home
Assistant (Home Dashboard, Sun Tracking, Reset to Auto, ...), so keep
them fresh in the background whenever a MOCO_RS485 port is assigned,

The stylesheet inlining regex required <link rel="stylesheet" href="..."> to
end right after href, but data/index.html's tags gained a data-boot-retry
