notes.summary: feat: periodic MoCo real-position auto-refresh for gateway reads; document Home Assistant gateway
notes.body:
Zones with a real MoCo-RS485 position readback mapping now get their
currentPosition/currentTiltAngle refreshed automatically in the background
(~45s interval) whenever a BACnet, KNX, or Home Assistant gateway is active,
so gateway reads reflect real hardware state instead of only
automation-computed values - no gateway-side code changes needed, since all
three already read through the same getZoneCurrentPositionAngle() snapshot
this refresh feeds.

Also fully documents the Home Assistant MQTT gateway in CLAUDE.md (previously
undocumented despite being fully implemented) and fixes stale cross-references
in CLAUDE.md/docs/homeassistant-mqtt.md left over from the BACnet/KNX
standalone-page consolidation.

notes.summary: fix: an Apply & Restart on one page could kill an in-flight save on another
notes.body:
RS485 Ports/Network Config/Gateway Setting each reboot the device via their
own independent Apply & Restart flow, none of which checked whether some
other page's edit (e.g. a multi-step Number of Zones save, sent one file at
a time) was still mid-save. A real-hardware incident traced a vanished zone
back to exactly this: an Apply & Restart cut off an in-flight zone-creation
save, leaving a zoneIndex entry pointing at a file that was never written -
silently cleaned up by the existing repair-on-load logic much later, far
from the actual cause. All three now call the same save-then-verify guard
restartDeviceNow() already had, cancelling the restart instead of rebooting
over unsaved work.

notes.summary: feat: real motor position/tilt readback over RS485-between-Motor-Controllers
notes.body:
Adds an on-demand Set Address + Read Position protocol (reverse-engineered
by the user against real 4-motor MoCo hardware) so BuCo can query a MoCo's
actual position/tilt instead of only ever estimating it from the last-sent
command. Runs on the existing IbPlusTx task, resolves the MoCo-id-to-zone
mapping from moco-ids.json, and overwrites zone.currentPosition/
currentTiltAngle directly (per explicit product decision) so automation
follows real hardware state. MoCo ID page is now permanent (no longer
gated behind Advanced Settings) since its bookkeeping is load-bearing.
Confirmed working end to end on real hardware.

notes.summary: docs: add help content for Control/Area Control/Home/Alarm/Rain-Snow and unify Sensors help pages
notes.body:
Adds translated help modal content (en/cs/de/fr/hr/pl) for Zone Control, Area
Control, Home, Security -> Alarm and Security -> Rain/Snow, sourced from the
reference product's help text and adapted to this app's actual UI/behavior.

Renames the Zone/Area Control "Advanced" tab and badge to "Position" (with
translations) to better describe the exact-position screen.

Introduces two shared help pages, following the existing Log page precedent
(window.currentHelpPageId override in each view's init function):
- data/help/sensors.html for the top-level Sensors status dashboards
  (ADIO/DIO/RS485 live values).
- data/help/settings-sensors.html for the Settings -> Sensors configuration
  pages (ADIO/DIO/RS485 Configuration), replacing and translating the
  previously English-only rs485-config.html content.

notes.summary: feat: configurable RS485 port roles + RS485 between Motor Controllers
notes.body:
Which protocol runs on each of the two physical RS485 ports is now an
installer choice (Settings > Options > Basic Settings > RS485 Ports)
instead of a compile-time constant. Roles: None / IB+ / MoCo RS485 /
Somfy RS485 sensors. SDN and Modbus are deliberately not offered until
their firmware exists, so a role can never be selected that does nothing.

Both ports may drive motor controllers, including the same role twice:
IB+ has hard limits on cable length and unit count, so two independent
buses double one gateway's capacity. Only the sensors role is
single-port (one UART, one snapshot), enforced on read and on write.

New MoCo RS485 transport (4-motor IB+ controllers only) is a pure
wrapper around the unmodified IB+ telegram:

  B7 | LEN | ctrA | 10 | 70 | <complete IB+ telegram> | CRC2

so none of the ~48 queueIbPlus*() call sites changed and nothing in the
menus or control pages behaves differently. Derived from Somfy's own
IBMoCoMessage() and verified byte-for-byte against 19 frames captured
from a real bus by a host-compiled harness.

writeTelegramToAllMotorPorts() writes to every port first and only then
flushes them all - the ports are independent UARTs, so two buses cost
the same wall-clock time as one. Nothing is started for an unselected
role: with no motor port, IbPlusTx is never created; with no sensor
port, neither is SensorBusTask.

Two defects found on real hardware during bring-up:

- The UART must follow the ROLE, not the port number. Tidying the
  mapping to port1->Serial1/port2->Serial2 put IB+ on Serial2 at 300
  baud for the first time and it went completely silent, while the
  telegrams were still built and logged normally. A motor bus now
  always takes Serial1, the SensorBus always Serial2.
- MoCo RS485 line settings are 38400 8E1, not 4800 8O1 - the latter is
  Somfy SDN's, the two were swapped in the original spec. Same silent
  symptom: correct frame on the wire, no motor reacting.

Both control paths confirmed working on real hardware.

Also: rs485-ports.json joins the backup set and factory reset, the
MoCo Settings menu group hides when no port drives motors, RS485
Configuration warns when no port carries the sensors role, and the
now-wrong "second RS485 port" wording is corrected in all six locales.

notes.summary: docs: record the Up-button-stays-disabled limitation and why it's staying as-is
notes.body:
Root-caused from a live report: currentPosition/currentTiltAngle are only
ever written by zone_functions.cpp's automation Step B (an active
ZONE_FUNCTIONS watcher), never by any manual command path - browser Zone
Control, BACnet, KNX, or now MQTT all just send a raw telegram via
queueIbPlusGotoPos()/queueIbPlusCommand() with no position write-back, since
IB+ has no feedback to confirm one. A zone only ever operated manually
therefore keeps its seed-default position (0, "open") forever, and Home
Assistant correctly disables the now-redundant Open button based on that
stuck value - not a bug, just IB+'s lack of feedback surfacing visibly
through HA's cover UI in a way BACnet/KNX's plain point exposure never
showed.

Explicit user decision: leave the behavior as-is rather than adding
optimistic position tracking on manual commands - that would need to apply
to every gateway equally (not a quiet MQTT-only special case) to preserve
the "gateway command indistinguishable from a browser click" invariant, and
isn't fully accurate anyway (a Stop mid-travel would leave the wrong
optimistic value). Documented as a known limitation instead of silently
patched.

notes.summary: fix: Home Assistant discovery silently dropped points once the outbound queue filled
notes.body:
Real bug, found from a live report (only 4 of 8 configured zones ever
appeared in Home Assistant, discovery configs for zones 5-8 still showed
the OLD truncated payload from before the previous fix).

tickHaManager()'s discovery loop advanced g_discoveryPos unconditionally,
up to HA_DISCOVERY_BUDGET (10) points on every single loop() iteration -
loop() runs far faster than mqtt_client.cpp's own dedicated task can drain
and physically write the outbound queue (bounded to 8 drains per ~20ms
poll), so the queue (16 slots) filled almost immediately after connect.
Every mqttPublish() call after that returned false (queue full) and was
silently dropped - but g_discoveryPos kept advancing regardless, marking
those points as "already handled" even though nothing was ever sent for
them. Only the first ~16 slots' worth of points (zones 1-4, in point-table
order) ever actually got discovered; the rest were permanently skipped for
that connection.

State publishing never had this bug: publishHaPoint() already only updates
a point's hasValue/lastValue (the "still needs publishing" signal) on a
successful mqttPublish(), so a dropped state update self-heals on the next
sweep pass. Discovery's fire-and-forget shape was just missing the same
discipline.

Fixed by making every publish*Discovery() function (and
publishDiscoveryForPoint()) return whether its mqttPublish() actually
enqueued. tickHaManager()'s loop now only advances g_discoveryPos on
success and stops the whole loop for that tick on the first failure,
retrying the exact same point next tick - naturally throttling to the
queue's real drain rate instead of racing ahead of it and dropping the
overflow.

Re-verified on real hardware: all 8 configured zones now show complete,
valid discovery JSON on the broker and all 8 came back from Home
Assistant's own /api/states as real cover entities. Also confirmed, while
investigating the same report, that the reported "Stop doesn't work" and
"Up button missing" are NOT bugs: a real IB+ Cancel-Priority telegram
(08 52) was observed going out on STOP, and the disabled Up button is Home
Assistant correctly reflecting a never-driven zone's default raw position
(0, this codebase's own "open" convention) - it isn't a fixed value, it
just hasn't seen a real move yet.

notes.summary: fix: Home Assistant discovery JSON silently truncated to 40 bytes, no entity ever created
notes.body:
Real bug, found from a live report ("device shows up in HA MQTT integration
with 0 entities") and confirmed via Home Assistant's own log: "Unable to
parse JSON zone35: '{\"name\":\"Zone 4\",\"unique_id\":\"buco-0a0d'" - cut off
at exactly 40 characters, for every single discovery config.

PublishQueueEntry.payload (mqtt_client.cpp) shared MQTT_PAYLOAD_MAX (40B)
with the public MqttReceivedMessage struct - sized correctly for tiny STATE/
command payloads ("1", "OPEN", "75.50") but silently truncating every
discovery JSON blob (~550-650B for a cover's config) through mqttPublish()'s
own snprintf(entry.payload, sizeof(entry.payload), ...). State/command
publishing worked fine the whole time (small enough to fit); only discovery
was affected, and the previous day's "confirmed on real hardware" note in
docs/homeassistant-mqtt.md was wrong - it never actually checked payload
length, just eyeballed a terminal-truncated preview and assumed HA had
parsed it, which HA structurally could not have done.

Fixed with a NEW, separate MQTT_PUBLISH_PAYLOAD_MAX (768B) used only by
PublishQueueEntry and sendPublishRaw()'s internal buffer - deliberately kept
out of the public mqtt_client.h (MQTT_PAYLOAD_MAX stays 40B there) so
ha_manager.cpp's tickHaManager(), which stack-allocates
MqttReceivedMessage[8] on loopTask (a much tighter stack budget than the
dedicated MqttClient task), doesn't inherit a ~6KB stack cost it never
needs. MQTT_PUBLISH_QUEUE_SIZE lowered 48 -> 16 to keep the heap-allocated
queue's total size reasonable now that each slot is much bigger (~13.3KB
total, paid only while the gateway is enabled).

Re-verified end to end this time by querying Home Assistant's own
/api/states directly (not just mosquitto_sub) - 24 real entities came back,
including cover.buco_esp32_buco_0a0dad_zone_2 in state "open". Corrected
docs/homeassistant-mqtt.md's own now-known-wrong verification claim rather
than silently rewriting it, since the false positive is itself worth
remembering: a terminal-truncated preview is not the same as confirming the
consuming system actually parsed the full payload.

notes.summary: fix: Home Assistant switch commands never worked, cover/switch subscribes flooded receive queue
notes.body:
Two real bugs found from a live user report ("mosquitto_pub command did
nothing" / "Zone 2 switch not controllable"):

1. dispatchCommand() parsed switch command topics assuming
   "zone<id>/lock/set" (a slash), but the actual command_topic published in
   the switch's own discovery config is "zone<id>_lock/set" (an underscore -
   publishZoneLockDiscovery()/publishZoneSunDiscovery()'s own objectId is
   one combined "zone<id>_lock"/"zone<id>_sun" segment). A real Home
   Assistant switch click always publishes to the literal command_topic from
   its discovery config, so this meant Lock/Sun switch commands from the
   real HA UI could never have worked, full stop - an ad-hoc manual test
   during development used a hand-typed "zone<id>/sun/set" topic that only
   happened to match by accident, via the now-removed "switch/#" wildcard
   subscription (see bug 2), never the real command_topic shape.

2. The two SUBSCRIBE filters ("<nodeId>/cover/#"/"<nodeId>/switch/#") were
   too broad: "#" also matches this device's OWN state topics under the
   same prefix (position/tilt/lock/sun/status), which are retained. On every
   (re)connect the broker immediately echoed every one of those retained
   states straight back, instantly filling the 16-slot receive queue
   (confirmed on real hardware: ">> [ MQTT ]: Receive queue full - dropping
   oldest unread command." seconds after connect) and creating a real
   window where a genuine incoming command could be evicted before
   tickHaManager() ever drained it - dispatchCommand() already silently
   ignored anything not ending in "/set", so this was a queue-capacity bug,
   not a correctness one, but still a real to intermittently swallow a
   command sent shortly after (re)connect.

Fixed by subscribing to only the 4 real command-topic shapes via MQTT's
single-level "+" wildcard (matches one whole segment's content, underscores
included, so "<nodeId>/switch/+/set" alone covers both zone<id>_lock/set and
zone<id>_sun/set) instead of the broad "#" - the broker now never delivers a
state topic to this device at all, closing bug 2 structurally rather than
filtering after the fact. MQTT_MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS raised 4 -> 8 for headroom
(4 filters actually used).

Re-verified end to end on real hardware with the CORRECT topic shapes this
time (matching literally what a real HA discovery config declares): cover
STOP flipped the zone's Manual status, switch OFF flipped the Sun Protection
switch's own published state - both confirmed via mosquitto_sub, and no more
"Receive queue full" line in the boot log.

notes.summary: feat: add Home Assistant MQTT gateway, consolidate gateway selection into one page
notes.body:
Third optional network gateway alongside BACnet/KNX, mutually exclusive with
both. Hand-rolled MQTT 3.1.1 client (QoS 0 only, no TLS - src/ha_port/
mqtt_client.h/.cpp) since the vendor EQSP32 library's own MQTT/HA-Discovery
support is unusable here (part of the disableErqosIoT'd IoT core that starves
the W5500 driver on this board) and a TLS handshake was measured elsewhere on
this exact hardware at ~65-100KB transient heap - too risky against this
board's heap budget, and unnecessary for a broker on the same local network.

src/ha_manager.cpp mirrors bacnet_manager.cpp/knx_manager.cpp's point-table
discipline exactly: counting pre-pass then exact-size heap allocation, no
per-object heap cost, RAM-only command dispatch through the same
queueIbPlusCommand()/requestZoneManualPending() trio the other two gateways
use (an MQTT command is indistinguishable downstream from a browser click).
A zone's position+tilt+open/close/stop collapse into one native HA `cover`
entity instead of BACnet/KNX's separate AV+BV+command-point model; Lock and
Sun Protection enable become their own `switch` entities; status functions,
hardware pins, Weather Forecast and RS485 SensorBus readings become
sensor/binary_sensor entities via MQTT Discovery, published once at
(re)connect and never held resident in RAM afterward.

Verified safe on this board via a Phase 0 feasibility spike before writing
any production code (ha_port/ha_spike.h/.cpp, since removed): a persistent
plain-TCP MQTT connection costs only ~5-6KB transient heap per connect burst,
recovering within ~10s, no drift across repeated reconnects. Full stack
re-verified end to end against real hardware afterward (real zones, real
RS485 sensors, real Home Assistant instance) including a live command
round-trip in both directions. One real regression caught before it shipped:
the outbound/inbound MQTT queues were originally plain static arrays, costing
~8.4KB of RAM even with the gateway disabled - fixed to heap-allocate only
inside mqttClientInit(), same "disabled gateway costs zero bytes" rule
BACnet/KNX's own point tables already follow.

UI: per explicit user request, gateway enable/select moved off Advanced
Settings' two independent allowBacnetGateway/allowKnxGateway checkboxes (and
BACnet/KNX's separate standalone setting pages) onto a single Settings ->
Basic Settings -> Gateway page. First screen is a single choice (None/
BACnet/KNX/Home Assistant, default None); further screens show only the
selected gateway's own settings. Backed by one /network.json field,
activeGateway, replacing the two booleans - makes "more than one gateway
selected" structurally unrepresentable instead of merely prevented by a JS
handler. bacnet_manager.cpp/knx_manager.cpp's own flag readers now delegate
to network_config.h's getActiveGateway() instead of independently
re-parsing zones.json.

Also fixes a real, separately-reported bug in the same apply-and-restart
flow this touched: network-config.js/gateway-setting.js's Apply handlers
showed a permanent "Connection failed" whenever ESP.restart() cut the TCP
connection out from under an in-flight fetch() (confirmed via live testing -
the save had actually succeeded and the device was already back up and
running). Both now treat that race the same as the success path: wait for
the device to come back, then reload.

dev/homeassistant-test-stack/ adds a disposable local Mosquitto + Home
Assistant Docker stack for developing/testing this gateway without needing
a customer's real broker. docs/homeassistant-mqtt.md documents the topic
scheme, worked discovery examples, and open questions (LWT/retained-message
cleanup, tilt percent-to-degree mapping not yet UX-verified).

notes.summary: docs: record the Weather Forecast first-run seeding gap and its general rule
notes.body:
Documents the 2026-07-31 field report fixed in 7591247, next to the existing
"first run is a real 404 and nothing else" rule it is a corollary of: a loader
that seeds only into window.* leaves the firmware with nothing to read.

Both load-bearing claims were verified against the source before writing them
down: weather_manager.cpp hardcodes all five metrics into one Open-Meteo URL
and never consults /weather.json, and sensor_logger.cpp does read that file to
pick which metrics to sample - which is exactly why the file not existing meant
nothing was logged while the UI showed everything enabled.

Also states the general rule for future config files: if firmware reads it, the
first-run seed must be persisted, not just held in RAM.

notes.summary: fix: Weather Forecast metrics were configured but never actually logged
notes.body:
Field report: Weather Forecast turned on, the fetch visibly working, every
metric shown ticked on Settings -> Sensors -> Weather Forecast - and nothing
in Log -> Sensors, with no indication why. The serial log showed
"/littlefs/weather.json does not exist" on every sampling tick.

Two independent causes, both on the first-run path:

- /weather.json was only ever written once the installer happened to tick
  something on that page AND press Save. sensor_logger.cpp reads that file to
  decide which metrics to record, so until then it recorded none.
  loadWeatherConfig() now persists its seeded defaults straight away on a real
  404, exactly like loadHardwareConfig() already did. The save promise is
  returned so the next loader in the boot chain doesn't start while this POST
  is in flight (the "one request in flight at a time" rule), and a failure is
  swallowed so it can never block boot.

- ensureWeatherConfig() seeded every metric disabled, so even once the file
  existed it selected nothing. Seeded enabled instead: the feature already has
  its own master switch in Advanced Settings, and the device fetches all five
  metrics in one request regardless of which are ticked - so "on but recording
  nothing" was never a state worth defaulting to.

Per this project's no-migration rule both only affect a fresh seed; an
already-configured device keeps whatever its /weather.json says.

Needs `pio run -t uploadfs` to reach a device, like any data/ change.

notes.summary: perf: reclaim ~18KB static RAM + ~11KB heap across the whole firmware
notes.body:
RAM headroom, not any design decision, had become what limits this product:
the Weather fetch had to drop TLS to fit, the OTA check gates at 100KB free
heap and can never satisfy that on a low-headroom device, and BACnet needed
three re-engineering passes purely to keep free heap off the 40KB load-shed
floor at 24-32 zones. Measured the whole binary from the linker map first,
then fixed the biggest items. Static RAM 117396 -> 99112 B (35.8% -> 30.2%);
our own src/ went 40151 -> 23807 B.

Static (.bss/.data), all verified against the map:
- Per-zone arrays were sized ZONE_ID_BOUND (64) and indexed by the raw zoneId,
  but real zoneIds start at 32 - so slots 0..31 of all 37 of them were
  permanently unreachable. Added ZONE_ID_MIN/ZONE_SLOT_COUNT/zoneSlot() to
  zone_id_bound.h (which now also owns ZONES_MAX_COUNT, since the arrays are
  sized from it) and re-indexed every one. isValidZoneId() tightened to
  >= ZONE_ID_MIN, which is what makes zoneSlot() safe; it was already checked
  at every entry point, so no new validation was needed. -8352 B.
- ota_manager: the 4KB changelog buffer lived inside the permanently resident
  g_ota struct. Now heap, sized to the real measureJson() result, with a
  documented single-owner free() rule. -4092 B.
- bacnet: MAX_APDU 1476 -> 1024 (a standard BACnet enumeration, advertised in
  I-Am and Max_APDU_Length_Accepted, so it is a declared contract) and the
  1506 B PDUBuffer moved off .bss to a heap allocation made only once the
  gateway is actually enabled. -3310 B.
- email queues, event-log queue depth, sensor-logger key buffer. -2398 B.

Heap:
- async_tcp task stack 16KB -> 8KB via CONFIG_ASYNC_TCP_STACK_SIZE (confirmed
  0x2000 in the built ELF). Real hardware then measured 4872 B still free.
- SensorBusTask is no longer created unconditionally - only once an RS485
  device is actually configured, so installations without a weather station
  stop paying 4KB for it. Its stack went 4096 -> 5120 on the strength of a
  measured 1088 B worst-case headroom (and a duplicate #define was removed).
- Weather fetch task stack 10KB -> 4KB; it stopped needing a TLS handshake.

Fixes found along the way, not strictly memory:
- /api/ota-status built a ~4.3KB payload with beginResponseStream(), i.e. the
  throwing new char[] cbuf grow path that aborted the device in the documented
  2026-07-15 crash, and copied 4KB onto the async_tcp stack. Now chunked.
- The SMTP send opened a full STARTTLS session with no heap gate and no
  transient floor, unlike Weather and OTA which both got exactly that after
  real w5500_tsk panics - and an Error email fires unattended, so it can land
  mid-cold-load. Same gate added.
- The four schedule files each hold every zone's 7x6 slots, and were parsed
  whole once per zone; the "config changed" flag clears per sweep, not per
  zone, and starts true - so every boot did up to 32 full parses per file, x4
  files, exactly while browsers cold-load. Now parsed through an ArduinoJson
  Filter that keeps only the requested zone.
- -D DISABLE_SDCARD was a typo the library never checks; it is DISABLE_SD.
- setup()'s esp_log_level_set("vfs_api", ESP_LOG_NONE) never worked - proven
  by a serial capture still showing the full flood. vfs_api.cpp logs via
  Arduino's log_e(), which that API does not govern. Replaced with
  -D CORE_DEBUG_LEVEL=0 (also -30KB flash); dead call removed.

Not done, deliberately: lwIP/WiFi/mbedTLS buffer sizing is baked into the
prebuilt Arduino archives, so -D CONFIG_* flags there do nothing. Bluetooth
costs ~22KB (~5KB .bss plus ~17KB IRAM, which steals DRAM 1:1 on S3) for a
radio disableErqosIoT means we never use, but libEQSP32.a pulls NimBLE in and
only ERQOS can ship a build without it. Both recorded in CLAUDE.md.

Still to verify on hardware: the two-browser cold-load stress test at 32 zones
with a gateway on (the >> [ STACK ] line added here is the instrument), and
the e-mail gate thresholds, which are an estimate of the STARTTLS envelope
rather than a measurement.

notes.summary: fix: Weather Forecast never fetched - TLS heap cost exceeded device headroom
notes.body:
Root-caused (not another threshold guess): WiFiClientSecure's TLS session
for the HTTPS call to Open-Meteo transiently cost ~65-78KB regardless of
response size, and this device's idle heap (~82-93KB) never had enough
margin above that - confirmed real-hardware fetch on the new plain-HTTP
path. Live-verified api.open-meteo.com serves the identical JSON on plain
HTTP (port 80, no redirect), so fetchOpenMeteo() now uses a plain
WiFiClient + http:// instead of WiFiClientSecure + pinned CA. Shrank the
transient by an order of magnitude, letting WEATHER_MIN_FREE_HEAP/
_LARGEST_BLOCK drop from 100KB/48KB to 24KB/8KB with real margin.

Also caps bacnet-stack's Address_Cache (255 -> 16 entries via
MAX_ADDRESS_CACHE), found while auditing baseline RAM usage - it was
linked in and reserved unconditionally regardless of the BACnet gateway
toggle. Frees ~8.6KB either way (measured).

notes.summary: fix: revert Weather fetch heap thresholds to safe originals - crashed again
notes.body:
Two consecutive crash-loops on the real device confirmed the previous
fix's own root-cause theory was wrong. Both collapses (93872->15516 and
83588->19428 bytes free) happened with "HTTP in-flight: 0" logged for the
entire preceding 1.5-2 minutes - no concurrent browser burst to shed away,
contradicting the theory that motivated splitting the start gate from the
transient floor. The real mechanism: the fetch's own allocation alone
consumes ~74-78KB every time it runs (more than the ~65KB documented from
the original 2026-07-15 device), and this device's idle baseline is only
~82-93KB - leaving ~15-19KB afterward, below what the W5500 driver's own
receive-buffer allocation survives, with or without other HTTP traffic.

Lowering the start gate to 70KB/24KB didn't make the fetch "sometimes"
run - idle heap clears it on every single retry, so this produced "always
starts, always crashes" instead of the original "never starts, never
crashes". Strictly worse. Reverted WEATHER_MIN_FREE_HEAP/
WEATHER_MIN_LARGEST_BLOCK to the original 100KB/48KB and removed the
now-pointless separate transient-floor constants (both pairs are equal
again). The original "Weather Forecast never fetches on this device"
symptom is back, but a repeating crash-loop on a device that also drives
physical motors is categorically worse and must not be tolerated for the
sake of a nice-to-have feature.

A real fix needs to shrink the fetch's own ~65-78KB memory footprint (the
framework's WiFiClientSecure has no setBufferSizes() to reduce TLS buffer
allocation, so this needs real investigation) or reduce this build's
other baseline RAM usage - deliberately not attempted here; both need
careful, isolated testing rather than another quick threshold change.

notes.summary: fix: weather fetch's own load-shed protection was weakened by the last fix
notes.body:
Real crash on the very next boot after the previous commit confirmed the
mistake: it lowered BOTH the pre-fetch start gate AND the
httpLoadShedSetTransientFloor() reservation to the same 70KB/24KB pair.
That let the fetch start (fixing the original bug), but also weakened the
shed guard's protection *during* the fetch - a third concurrent browser
burst arrived mid-fetch and only got shed once heap had already collapsed
to ~17KB/7.6KB (guard floor was 70KB instead of the original 100KB, so it
let more of the burst through before shedding kicked in), triggering the
exact w5500_tsk stack-canary panic this mechanism exists to prevent.

These are two different concerns and must not share one pair of numbers:
WEATHER_MIN_FREE_HEAP/_LARGEST_BLOCK (now 70KB/24KB) only gate whether to
START a fetch, matching this device's genuinely lower idle baseline.
New WEATHER_TRANSIENT_FLOOR_FREE_HEAP/_LARGEST_BLOCK (100KB/48KB, the
original values) feed only the shed-guard reservation while the fetch is
in flight, so concurrent browser load still gets aggressively 503'd for
the fetch's ~14s worst case regardless of how low the idle heap that let
it start was.

notes.summary: fix: Weather fetch heap gate never satisfied on a device with lower idle heap
notes.body:
Confirmed via a real device's serial log (useWeatherForecast on for 8+
hours, never once fetched): idle free heap sits around ~80KB / largest
block ~47-49KB even with zero concurrent HTTP activity, below the
100KB/48KB minimums the fetch gate required - so it wasn't occasionally
deferred, it structurally could never run at all on this device. Those
minimums were calibrated against the 2026-07-15 incident's own device
state (~122-131KB idle). Lowered to 70KB/24KB, just under this device's
observed idle baseline, while keeping the layered protections that
actually excluded that incident's real trigger unchanged (in-flight==0
gate, boot warmup, transient floor reservation). Needs real-hardware
confirmation that a fetch now completes without recurring the w5500
panic those protections exist to prevent.

notes.summary: feat: Log -> Sensors chart gets granularity switch, pan slider, center crosshair
notes.body:
Replaces free wheel/pinch zoom with a guided Hour/Day/Week/Month switch -
each mode has a fixed, always-odd point count (5/97/169/31) so the window
is always centered on a real data point; Week/Month bucket the raw 15-min
records into 1h/1day min-of-mins/max-of-maxes buckets client-side (no API
change). A scrollbar-style slider below the chart pans the window, its
thumb width reflecting how much of the total stored history is currently
visible; both the slider and canvas drag-pan quantize to the current
mode's step (15min/1h/1day). A fixed crosshair at the chart's horizontal
center shows the value(s) - one if min===max for that point, otherwise
max+min - and timestamp of whichever point is centered.

notes.summary: fix: Weather Forecast stayed reported as disabled/offline after its gate cleared
notes.body:
tickWeatherManager() only ever set fetchState explicitly to WX_DISABLED/
WX_OFFLINE; once the toggle was turned back on (or connectivity returned),
a heap/in-flight fetch deferral could return without ever refreshing that
label, so /api/weather-status kept reporting the stale state indefinitely
even though the real gate no longer applied and no fetch had ever actually
been attempted (confirmed live: advancedSettings.useWeatherForecast=true,
state still "disabled", lastFetchAgeSec=-1). Clear the stale label back to
WX_NEVER_FETCHED as soon as its gate passes. Also fixed the demo's mocked
weather-status route, which read a nonexistent weather.json field instead
of the real zones.json gate.

notes.summary: fix: Locals page silently re-detected language via IP on every visit
notes.body:
initLocalsView() re-ran silent IP auto-detect whenever the current
language happened to be "en" - so an explicit choice of English kept
getting overwritten by the IP lookup's guess on the next visit. Track
whether the language has ever been explicitly resolved (boot language
gate, a manual Locals choice, or a completed detect) via a new
localeSettings.languageAutoDetected flag instead, so auto-detect only
ever fires once, regardless of which language it lands on.

notes.summary: feat: RS485 sensors selectable in Log -> Sensors/Export
notes.body:
Firmware already logged every enabled RS485 SensorBus channel into the
history accumulators, but collectLoggableSensors() (the shared catalog
behind both pages' sensor dropdowns) never walked the RS485 sensor list,
so no RS485 sensor could actually be picked despite its history being
recorded. Adds RS485 entries via getAllRs485SensorEntries(), with
client-side unit scaling (Klux/km/h) to match the live RS485 status page
since that history is stored raw.

notes.summary: feat: RS485 SensorBus units on status page + swap SensorBus/IB+ ports
notes.body:
Confirmed against a real animeo Compact Sensor: sun channels read Lux,
wind-speed channels read m/s. Sensors -> RS485 status now converts these
(Klux, Locale wind/temp unit preference) via a new evaluateRs485SensorValue(),
instead of showing bare numbers.

Swapped which RS485 port each protocol uses: IB+ now runs on the second
driver (former CAN H/CAN L terminals), SensorBus now runs on the original
port (labeled TxD/RxD) - lets the installer route wires more directly.
Only the EQ_RS485_*/EQ_RS485_2_* pin macros passed into each module's
init moved; baud/frame stay tied to the protocol.

Also tried and reverted allowing the Outside Sensor Box Extension to pair
with animeo Compact/M8/M13 - the user confirmed the Extension can only be
physically connected to the base Outside Sensor Box.

notes.summary: fix: bootstrap-icons webfont could get 503-shed with no retry, unlike its own CSS
notes.body:
The <link>-level boot-retry mechanism only reacts to a DOM error event on the
element it's attached to; a font file fetched internally by the CSS engine
because of an @font-face rule never fires one, so a shed font request under
low heap left every icon as a permanent empty box with no recovery. Added an
independent Font Loading API based retry that re-fetches just the two font
files and registers them via document.fonts.add() once loaded.

notes.summary: fix: KNX point table was reserving worst-case RAM unconditionally at boot
notes.body:
g_knxPoints[] was a fixed static array (~684 entries, ~10.7KB) always
reserved in BSS regardless of allowKnxGateway or actual zone count -
the same rejected shape BACnet's own point-table fix (bacnet_zone_objects)
moved away from today. Now heap-allocated once, sized exactly via a
counting pre-pass across zones/sensors/weather/RS485, so a disabled
gateway costs zero bytes and an enabled one pays only for what it uses.

notes.summary: fix: boot/view script retry logic dropped stragglers, leaving a permanent tombstone
notes.body:
index.html's boot-script recovery batched near-simultaneous <script> failures
by snapshotting pendingScriptFailures at schedule time - any script that
failed while an earlier retry was already pending got queued but never
actually retried, permanently abandoned. On real hardware (32 zones + BACnet
cold boot) 4 of 5 boot scripts 503'd together; only the first got retried,
so app.js never loaded and the UI hung on "Setting up the gateway..." forever.

Separately, loadView()/wizard.js/update-motor-controllers.js each duplicated
the same view-module script loader with an analogous bug: the <script> tag
was marked data-loadview at creation time instead of on successful load, so
a shed 503 left a permanent "already loaded" tombstone - the next visit to
that page skipped straight to the init callback with no working module
behind it (confirmed: Home's zone tiles never rendered, "initHomeView not
found" on every subsequent visit until a hard reload). Extracted a shared
loadModuleScript() helper that only marks data-loadview after a real onload
and retries with backoff on failure, used by all three call sites.

notes.summary: fix: critical regression - runBootChain() was crashing on every single page load
notes.body:
A screen recording of a real device appeared to show the page reloading too
fast to ever finish loading. Root cause: the previous commit's
document.readyState-aware boot trigger called runBootChain() SYNCHRONOUSLY
in its else branch - but a <script defer> never actually observes
readyState === 'loading' by the time it executes at all (defer scripts only
run once parsing has finished), so that branch was taken on every load, not
just a retry, and it fired before several of this same script's own
module-level let/const declarations further down the file had executed.

Confirmed via console: "Uncaught ReferenceError: Cannot access
'headerDateTimePollHandle' before initialization" on every attempt - and
because this was an uncaught exception during the script's own synchronous
execution, it halted the rest of the file from running at all, which is
also why ZONE_FUNCTIONS then showed the same error from deep in the async
boot chain (a downstream symptom, not a second bug). The deterministic
crash kept re-arming bootConfigReloadCount's reload timer every ~5-11s
against a condition that could never resolve - indistinguishable from
"reloading too fast," with zero relation to actual server-side heap.

Fixed by deferring via setTimeout(runBootChain, 0) instead of calling it
inline, guaranteeing the whole script has finished executing first,
regardless of which branch is taken.

notes.summary: fix: retry only the specific failed boot script/stylesheet instead of reloading the page
notes.body:
Real-hardware retest showed app.js itself getting 503-shed as a <script>
tag (so nothing living inside it - fetchWithRetry, the visibility pause -
could help), and the old whole-page-reload recovery was self-perpetuating:
every automatic reload re-opens a brand-new ~6-connection cold-load burst,
so each retry has its own independent chance of re-tripping the shed
guard. Observed shedding recurring in waves across ~5 minutes as a result.

index.html now retries only the specific <script>/<link> that failed, in
place, with backoff - already-succeeded resources are never touched again.
Preserves the boot scripts' declaration-order execution guarantee across
retries (async=false, re-inserted in original relative order) without ever
re-running an already-successful script (these files use top-level
let/const, which throws on double execution).

Two companion correctness fixes in app.js, both required for this to work
at all: runBootChain() is now document.readyState-aware, since a script
that only succeeds on a delayed retry loads after DOMContentLoaded has
already fired; waitForI18nReady() guards the one residual ordering gap
(i18n.js alone failing while app.js succeeds) since loadI18nDictionaries is
the very first thing the boot chain calls.

bootResourceReloadCount/sessionStorage are gone from index.html entirely -
nothing reloads the page anymore, so there's nothing to persist.

notes.summary: fix: pause background pollers when tab is hidden, raise cold-load retry budgets
notes.body:
Real-hardware retest after the BACnet heap fix showed idle heap now clears
the load-shed floor comfortably, yet the web UI still sometimes never
finished loading even minutes after heap had settled. Browser DevTools
confirmed genuine sustained 503s outlasting the old retry budgets (~19-20s
fetchWithRetry, ~35s index.html reload counter) against measured shed
bursts up to ~45s - and closing an old, still-open background tab (not
anything server-side) was what let a fresh load succeed, since none of
app.js's "whole app lifetime" pollers (header date/time, header error
badge, zone-state) ever paused just because a tab wasn't visible.

Adds a single visibilitychange listener to pause/resume those three
pollers, and raises all three layered retry/reload budgets (fetchWithRetry,
bootConfigReloadCount, index.html's bootResourceReloadCount) to comfortably
outlast the worst burst actually measured.

notes.summary: fix: size BACnet AV/BV allocation to exact real point count, not a per-zone ceiling
notes.body:
Real-hardware retest (8/12/24/32 zones, BACnet on) showed only partial
improvement from the previous commit: BacnetZoneObjects_Init(zoneCount) still
sized each allocation as zoneCount x 19 (worst case for a zone with every
security function enabled), roughly 2x the real need for a default zone
(~9 BVs, since only manual/lock/error are non-"unused" by default) - leaving
idle free heap hovering right at the HTTP load-shed guard's 40KB floor.

buildBacnetObjectList() now runs a counting-only pass over every zone file
first (the same state != "unused" check the populating pass makes, just
tallied) to compute the exact AV/BV total, then calls the renamed
BacnetZoneObjects_Init(analogCapacity, binaryCapacity) with those exact
numbers before the populating pass runs. Each zone file is read twice at
boot instead of once - a small one-time cost for an allocation with no
slack at all.

notes.summary: fix: stop reserving worst-case BACnet AV/BV RAM unconditionally at boot
notes.body:
The previous commit's fixed-size static point tables (sized for 32 zones)
were reserved in BSS regardless of whether the BACnet gateway was enabled or
how many zones existed - confirmed on real hardware immediately after
flashing: a fresh, BACnet-disabled device lost ~30KB of RAM it never used to
lose, worse than the original incident.

Switches both tables to a single heap allocation per type, done once via
BacnetZoneObjects_Init(zoneCount) sized to the real zone count and called
only from buildBacnetObjectList() (which itself only runs when the gateway
is enabled) - restores zero cost when disabled while keeping the actual fix
(one bulk allocation instead of one calloc per object).

notes.summary: fix: eliminate BACnet gateway's per-zone heap cost via zero-heap AV/BV object provider
notes.body:
Real-hardware test sweep (8/12/24/32 zones with BACnet enabled) confirmed the
2026-07-19 status-BV mitigation wasn't enough: every AV/BV was still a
calloc'd bacnet-stack struct (~120B, never freed, scaling linearly with zone
count), pinning idle free heap at/below the HTTP load-shed guard's 40KB floor
at 24-32 zones and permanently wedging the web UI behind 503s after boot.

Replaces av.c/bv.c (removed from the build entirely) with
src/bacnet_zone_objects.h/.cpp - a project-owned provider backed by two flat,
fixed-capacity arrays (no calloc/new/strdup), mirroring the same
zero-heap-table pattern the KNX gateway already uses. RAM cost is now a fixed
~13.5KB of BSS regardless of configured zone count, instead of ~30-40KB of
heap that grew with it. Property lists, Min/Max/Out_Of_Service/Units
semantics, and the 100*order+offset instance numbering are all preserved
1:1, so the EDE file and existing BMS integrations need no changes.

notes.summary: feat: add DIO-triggered device reset/restart, simplify Test Zone Priority to whole-installation-only
notes.body:
Extracts factory-reset logic into device_reset.h/.cpp so it can be shared
between /api/reset and a new DIO switch trigger (device_reset/device_restart),
used to reproduce boot/heap states on demand during hardware testing.
Test Zone Priority DIO switches drop their per-Zone/Area target (matching
Test Bus Wires' existing whole-installation-only precedent) since a
dedicated target never made sense for a diagnostic-style switch.

notes.summary: fix: split Sun function enable into separate installer/user flags
notes.body:
Zone Control's "Sun function" toggle no longer touches
functions.sunProtection.state (the installer's own Comfort -> Sun
enable checkbox) - it now flips a new, independent userEnabled flag
instead, so a user without access to Settings can still turn Sun
automation off (and back on) for themselves without depending on the
installer's configuration. Both flags must be true for the Sun watcher
to actually run. BACnet/KNX's ENABLE_DISABLE_SUN_PROTECTION command
point is repointed to the same userEnabled flag (via
requestSunProtectionEnable()), since a BMS write is meant to act like
the end user's own toggle, not like an installer reconfiguring Comfort
-> Sun.

notes.summary: feat: add Sun function On/Off toggle to Zone Control
notes.body:
Shown only when Sun Protection is enabled for the selected zone; flips
the same functions.sunProtection.state field the BACnet/KNX
ENABLE_DISABLE_SUN_PROTECTION command point and the Sun settings page's
own enable checkbox already use.

notes.summary: feat: add User Management step to Configuration Wizard; docs: Tahoma gateway feasibility notes
notes.body:
Wizard now walks installers through account setup right before the final
Save Changes step, reusing the existing User Management page/JS unchanged;
loadWizardStep() now applies i18n translations to injected step markup so
that page's translated wrapper text renders correctly.

CLAUDE.md also records the Tahoma Gateway feasibility investigation
(no API-based device registration exists in TaHoma; not pursued).

notes.summary: feat: two-phase 90-deg reference-angle GOTO_POS for automated slat sends
notes.body:
Mechanical backlash/play and motor tilt-timing imprecision mean a slat
product's real physical angle after a GOTO_POS isn't reproducible when
approached from an arbitrary current angle. Every automated (non-manual)
GOTO_POS with an angle, on a slat-capable product, now closes to a fixed
90-deg reference first, waits Tilt Time + Backslash + (Start Delay Time for
Electronic motors) + (Slack Time when enabled), then sends the real target -
so the angle is always measured from the same starting point.

Covers regular ZONE_FUNCTIONS activate/deactivate (Step B), Sun Tracking's
continuous redrive, Sun Protection's Pre Open Slats, Timer's Single Event,
and Reset to Auto's post-reset restore. Manual Zone/Area Control and
BACnet/KNX writes are unaffected.

notes.summary: fix: rebuild full changelog history from private repo tags, not the public record
notes.body:
changelog-full.json/dist/changelog.html were reconstructed by replaying the
public flasher checkout's own changelog.json history - but that history was
already capped at 10 notes total the instant a release was first published,
so a release with more raw commits than that (v1.0.103: 38, v1.0.122: 12)
could never be recovered in full that way. Now rebuilt straight from this
repo's own v<version> tags + git log between them (scripts/changelog_notes.py,
shared with make_factory_image.py's draft so the two logics can't drift
apart again), with a narrow fallback to the public record only for v1.0.35
(hand-written before this mechanism existed, no earlier tag to diff from).

Also captures each commit's full body (trailer stripped) alongside its
summary, rendered as an expandable <details>/<summary> per note in both
dist/changelog.html and the flasher site's Changelog card - the device-facing
changelog.json keeps summaries only.

notes.summary: feat: add plain Restart button, rename System Settings page to Restart / Reset
notes.body:
Adds a non-destructive device restart alongside the existing factory
reset, reusing the already-existing POST /api/restart route and the
shared waitForDeviceReboot() poll/reload helper.

notes.summary: fix: shorten Test Bus Wires cycle timing from 4s to 3s
notes.body:
Applies to both the browser-driven cycle (test-bus-wires.js) and the
DIO-switch-driven firmware cycle (bus_wires_test_engine.cpp), which are
meant to look identical on the bus.

notes.summary: feat: full-history changelog on flasher site + SharePoint export, release pipeline script
notes.body:
changelog-full.json (unbounded, bootstrapped losslessly from the flasher
repo's own git history) feeds a new progressive "Changelog" card on the
flasher install page and scripts/changelog_html.py's standalone
dist/changelog.html export - the device-side changelog.json stays capped at
10 notes as before. Also adds scripts/release_pipeline.py, chaining
merge_dev_to_main.py -> make_factory_image.py -> publish_flasher.py ->
push_flasher.py -> changelog_html.py -> make_demo.py in one run.

notes.summary: feat: DIO-triggered function switches for Test Zone Priority/Test Bus Wires/Sun & Timer Automatic
notes.body:
Lets an installer wire a physical switch to trigger Test Zones' 10s
Priority Down/Up/Cancel Priority & Unlock, Test Bus Wires' Start/Stop
(now whole-installation-only, no zone/area picker), and Sun/Timer
Automatic's On/Off - each edge-triggered (rising edge only), targeting
a Zone or an Area (the default "All Zones" area gives whole-
installation behavior via a single broadcast telegram, reusing the
Area fan-out plumbing Blind Buttons already use). No Toggle action -
tried and removed the same day after a real-hardware report where
Test Bus Wires' own repeating ON/OFF blink pulse (unrelated to any
toggle) was mistaken for one.

New src/bus_wires_test_engine.h/.cpp replicates the browser Test Bus
Wires page's blink cycle in firmware (a hardware switch has no
browser to run that JS), ticked directly from main.cpp's loop().

Several real-hardware bugs found and fixed during iterative testing:
- switches-dio.js stored a DIO field's zone/area target as the
  dropdown's raw string instead of a number: ArduinoJson's
  `config["zoneId"] | 0` silently returns 0 (invalid) for a JSON
  string, so any Zone/Area DIO type whose value was ever changed via
  the dropdown (not left at its auto-assigned default) never actually
  fired - affects Lock Zone/Area Dry Contact and Blind Button
  zone-target too, not just this feature.
- Area target "All Zones" was fanning out one telegram per real zone
  instead of a single broadcast (zoneId 0) for Test Zone Priority.
- tickBusWiresTest() originally ran from tickZoneFunctionsEngine()'s
  sweep-tail (once per completed sweep) - fine for Heartbeat's loose
  60s interval, but this installation's real sweep-completion cadence
  turned out to be ~7s, doubling the intended 4s step interval.
- Test Bus Wires' cycle had ON+OFF paired with the keep-alive sent
  alone; corrected to ON alone, then OFF paired with the keep-alive.
- requestBusWiresTestStop() only stopped future cycle steps, never
  sent the 09 2C "stop blinking" telegram itself - now sends it twice,
  matching test-bus-wires.js's twStopTest().

Also: human-readable Event Log labels for the 08 54/08 55 telegrams
(previously fell through to raw hex), and Live Value display for all
new DIO switch types on the Sensors -> DIO dashboard.

notes.summary: feat: explicit "Don't show again" checkbox on Welcome Screen
notes.body:
Persisting welcomeSeen used to be an implicit side effect of clicking
"Run Setup Wizard" - but the screen's own text invites skipping the
Wizard via the sidebar instead, and that path never persisted
anything, so the screen kept reappearing on every load/browser unless
the Wizard button was clicked. Replaced with an explicit checkbox that
is now the sole trigger for persisting the flag, decoupled from
whichever way the installer actually leaves the screen. Translated
into all 6 languages.

notes.summary: feat: percentage progress bar on the global Save overlay
notes.body:
32-zone saves take ~1 minute with only a spinner and no feedback, so the
user has no way to tell the save hasn't hung. Reuses #boot-overlay's
existing progress-bar CSS (generalized .boot-progress-* to .progress-*)
and drives it from performGlobalSave()'s own sequential save-chain index -
purely client-side, no firmware changes.

notes.summary: fix: Blind Button UP/DOWN pre-pass swallowed same-tick crossovers and release-from-Stop
notes.body:
The zone/area button pair state machine only fired UP/DOWN when the
previous sample was a clean "nothing pressed" - so a fast UP<->DOWN
crossover landing in the same ~1s poll (1->2/2->1), or releasing one
button after a brief accidental both-pressed Stop while still holding
the other (3->1/3->2), silently sent nothing. Generalized the rule to
key only on the current combined state, confirmed fixed on real
hardware. Also adds a transition-triggered ">> [ BTN DEBUG ]" log line
for future diagnosis.

notes.summary: fix: send End Limit Switch telegram unconditionally, default it on
notes.body:
Real hardware confirmed: Update Motor Controllers sent a correct Switch
Config telegram (08 11) but the motor controller silently ignored it,
because the End Limit Switch telegram (0A 4B) that every MoCo Config Tool
reference capture always pairs with Switch Config was gated behind a global
Advanced Settings toggle defaulting to off. Removed that toggle entirely per
the user's own decision; End Limit Switch is now an always-visible per-zone
checkbox (Run/Tilt Times -> Switch Config), defaulting on for new zones to
match the MoCo Config Tool's own default. Already-persisted zones keep their
old value - no migration, per this project's pre-deployment convention.

notes.summary: fix: Venetian blinds never get a Switch Config telegram when unset
notes.body:
A zone switched from a fixed-code product (e.g. Screen) to a plain Venetian
blind kept switchConfigValue at null forever, so Update Motor Controllers
built no Switch Config telegram at all and the motor controller stayed in
whatever mode a prior manual session had left it in - confirmed from a real
serial log with no 08 11/08 12/08 13/09 4E line anywhere. Added
RTT_SWITCH_CONFIG_DEFAULTS (Venetian blinds default to EU) as a render/send-
time fallback that never writes zone.switchConfigValue itself, so it can't
reintroduce the 2026-07-16 stamp-on-render incident. Window/arm-awning
products deliberately keep no default, per that same incident. Help text
updated and translated into all 6 languages from the start this time.

notes.summary: fix: welcomeSeen/disclaimer flag can silently fail to persist; prevent duplicate Blind Button assignment
notes.body:
closeWelcomeScreen()/acceptDisclaimer() saved their flag with a single-attempt
POST; a transient failure (load-shed 503, "another save in progress" 500)
left welcomeSeen stuck false on the device, so a later browser/session would
re-show the Welcome Screen even though it was already dismissed elsewhere.
Now retries a few times and falls back to markConfigDirty('container') so
the flag rides along on the next successful save either way.

Also stops two DIO pins from being assigned the same Blind Button
target (e.g. two "Zone 1 UP" pins) - firmware already ORs them together
per-target, which was silently confusing rather than blocked. The config UI
now disables already-taken zone/area options and refuses a type change with
no free target left.

notes.summary: fix: Screen/roller products never got a Switch Config telegram
notes.body:
buildRttTelegrams() gated the Switch Config branch on !excluded, but Screen
and its sibling roller-style products are members of RTT_EXCLUDED_PRODUCTS
with no dropdown entry either, so Update Motor Controllers never reconfigured
the physical wall button's ergonomics for them. Added a fixed-code product
group (Screen, Zip Screen, Roller Shutter, Interior Roller blind, Interior
PlisseĂ©, Markisolette, Interior Curtain) that always sends the Screen code,
and gave Fold/Drop arm awning the Deadman/Screen dropdown the original spec
called for. Help text updated and translated into all 6 languages.

notes.summary: feat: gate stale KNX GA export; add boot loading percentage readout
notes.body:
Export Group Addresses (CSV) is disabled whenever the exported addresses
could differ from what the device is actually running (unapplied edits on
this page, or a restart pending from a zone/hardware change elsewhere) -
KNX's point table is only rebuilt at boot. Also adds a lightweight
percent-complete indicator to the boot overlay so a slow initial load
doesn't look stuck; tracked via two plain counters, no history kept.

notes.summary: fix: shorten command-busy overlay to match faster IB+ send time
notes.body:
COMMAND_BUSY_MS was still sized for the old ~900ms triple-send (2500ms =
900ms send + ~1s tick-engine follow-up + margin). Now that ib_plus.cpp
sends each telegram once (~250-350ms, see 68e740c), the overlay lingered
far longer than the actual command took. Shortened to 1800ms using the
same margin logic with the new send time.

notes.summary: perf: send each IB+ telegram once instead of 3x
notes.body:
Passively listening to a real BuCo Premium/Touch BuCo installation (via a
Somfy RS485 monitor, since our own gateway has no IB+ receive path of its
own) showed every observed telegram carries a distinct, non-repeating
counter - those reference devices send each command exactly once. The
triple-send in ib_plus.cpp was unverified defensive redundancy, not a
protocol requirement, so removing it roughly triples command throughput
(the ~900ms per-telegram floor at 300 baud drops to ~250-350ms).

Also documents the abandoned attempt to build our own passive IB+ capture
tool: several generic USB-RS485 listeners (pyserial, various baud/parity/
RTS-DTR combinations) all received zero bytes even on wiring confirmed
live moments earlier via Somfy's own tool, pointing at vendor-specific
adapter direction control a generic serial library can't replicate.

notes.summary: feat: KNX security status heartbeat toggle; fix header i18n race, KNX RX diagnostics, Position DPT export
notes.body:
- KNX Gateway Setting is now a 2-tab carousel: Group Addresses (existing)
  and a new Security Status screen with an off-by-default checkbox that
  additionally force-republishes every enabled security-category function's
  status (Alarm/Lock/Error/Wind/Rain-Snow-Frost-Ice/Lock Timer) once a
  minute, on top of the existing change-of-value publish + ~10min full
  resync. Network Config and BACnet Gateway Setting updated to round-trip
  the new /network.json field verbatim, per this page family's existing
  pass-through rule.
- KNX RX debug logging now prints the raw HEX of every received datagram
  and a specific decode-failure reason (was one generic message for all 11
  validation checks) - used to confirm the recurring 14/22-byte frames are
  unrelated KNXnet/IP discovery traffic, not malformed ETS writes.
- Logs the Ethernet/AP IP at KNX multicast join time, for correlating
  against a packet capture on the suspected wrong-interface risk.
- Fixed header "User Management off" text showing in the browser's guessed
  language instead of the device's saved language (auth.js's
  renderHeaderUserStatus() was never re-invoked after the real dictionary
  loads).
- Fixed KNX Group Address CSV export tagging Position as DPT 5.003 instead
  of 5.001 (Angle correctly stays 5.003).

notes.summary: feat: mandatory first-boot language + disclaimer gate, synced to flasher site
notes.body:
Adds a language-selection step (dropdown, since the list will grow well
past today's 6 languages) followed by a mandatory liability-disclaimer
acceptance step before the app can be used, gating all sidebar navigation
and the Welcome screen until accepted - needed ahead of wider distribution
to installers/customers. Acceptance persists to the shared container
(disclaimerAccepted/Version/At) and re-prompts fleet-wide whenever
DISCLAIMER_VERSION is bumped. The canonical legal text
(data/legal/disclaimer-en.html, disclaimer-cs.html) is shared by the boot
gate, a new read-only Settings -> Options -> Disclaimer page, and - via a
new sync step in scripts/publish_flasher.py - the public flasher site's own
every-time acceptance gate, so there is exactly one copy of the text.

Also removes the Welcome screen's unused "Go to Home" button and expands
its body text to mention the sidebar menu as an alternative to the Wizard.

This disclaimer text is a drafted starting point for BAEE/Business Line
legal counsel, not a reviewed liability shield - see the open questions
called out in CLAUDE.md's "Disclaimer / legal" section.

notes.summary: fix: browser demo missing User Management API mocks
notes.body:
/api/session, /api/users, /api/login etc. aren't save-shaped, so they
fell through to the demo's generic /api/* fallback and broke the User
Management page (/api/users came back as {} instead of an array).
Added dedicated session/login/roles handlers to demo_runtime.js
mirroring user_manager.cpp, plus users.json/rs485.json to the demo's
backup file list and network.json to its reset handler.

notes.summary: feat: merge KNX Up/Down into DPT 1.008 point, retag Stop/Angle/Position DPTs
notes.body:
At the installer's request, matches the real-world KNX Shutter Actuator
convention more closely: Up and Down are now one DPT 1.008 (Up/Down) point
per zone (write 0 = Up, 1 = Down) instead of two separate momentary points,
dropping KNX_ZONE_POINTS_PER_ZONE from 21 to 20. Stop keeps its own point
and name but is also tagged DPT 1.008 (that convention's "Stop/Step
Up/Down" object) - this bus has no directional step, so any write still
just sends the single Stop telegram. My Position moves from DPT 1.010 to
1.001. Position/Angle are now tagged DPT 5.003 (Angle) instead of 5.001
(Scaling) in the exported CSV - the wire payload is unchanged either way
(both are the same 1-byte 0-255 raw value), so this is a CSV-label-only
change with no firmware encoding change.

notes.summary: feat: split BACnet/KNX Gateway Setting into own pages; fix KNX ETS CSV export + restart flag
notes.body:
BACnet Device ID/port and KNX Individual Address/Group Address base fields
move out of Network Config's own carousel tabs into two standalone pages
(Basic Settings, right after Network Config) - nobody found the KNX tab
buried inside Network Config. All three pages still share /network.json
(the save route writes the body verbatim, no server-side merge), so each
now loads and resends the other pages' fields unchanged. Added an inline
"unapplied changes" note next to each page's own Apply button, since none
of them use the header Save flow.

Rewrote the KNX Group Address CSV export to the tab-separated, headerless,
three-level Main/Middle/GroupAddress hierarchy ETS6 actually imports
(confirmed against a real ETS6 project export) - the old flat comma CSV
with a header row was rejected outright. Renamed the KNX base fields to
Zones/ADIO/DIO sensors/WF sensors/RS485 sensors.

Fixed the header Restart-required flag never triggering for KNX (only
allowBacnetGateway was checked, not allowKnxGateway).

Added temporary KNX RX debug logging (src/knx_manager.cpp) for diagnosing
a real ETS6 Group Monitor Write/Read report.

notes.summary: feat: User Management phone name, email warning, simple passwords; Network Config DHCP readout
notes.body:
- Header user indicator: show the signed-in name (clipped to ~5 chars)
  alongside the icon on phones too, instead of icon-only.
- User Management page: warn inline under the enable checkbox when
  Email Notification isn't usable (not enabled, or no SMTP host) -
  without it, password-reset codes can never be delivered. Links
  straight to the Email Notification page. Not a popup, per request.
- Drop the 8-character minimum on every password path (change/reset/
  save-user) - simple passwords are allowed now, only "non-empty" is
  still enforced.
- Network Config: DHCP mode now shows a read-only IP Address field
  with the live leased address (same cache the header's Eth status
  reads). Subnet Mask/Gateway are not shown in DHCP mode - the EQSP32
  vendor library (precompiled, no source) exposes no getter for the
  DHCP-negotiated values, only the current IP.

notes.summary: feat: always show a state in the header User Management indicator
notes.body:
Previously status-item-user was display:none whenever User Management
was off or only an implicit-admin session existed, leaving an empty
gap in the header (most noticeable on phones, where every other status
item is icon-only). Now it always shows something: a muted
shield-slash "off" icon + translated "User Management off" label when
there's nothing real to show, swapped to the usual person icon + the
signed-in name once a real session exists.

notes.summary: fix: surface expired/missing session on IB+ command routes
notes.body:
Every command-sending fetch() (/api/command, /api/goto_pos,
/api/zone_value, /api/learn_command, /api/energy_mode) used a bare
fetch() that never inspected the response status, so a 401 from the
User Management AuthGuard was silently swallowed - a button click
produced no telegram and no feedback at all, with nothing to explain
why (2026-07-24 field report: enabling User Management on an
already-open tab left it sending unauthenticated commands that just
did nothing until a fresh page load elsewhere forced a real login).

Adds fetchCommand() in app.js, mirroring fetchWithRetry()/
postJsonWithTimeout()'s existing 401 handling (calls
window.__handleSessionExpired() to reopen the login overlay), and
switches all 17 call sites over to it. Server-side authorization is
unchanged - firmware automation and BACnet/KNX writes never go
through this HTTP path at all, so they're unaffected either way.

notes.summary: feat: show Ethernet IP in mobile header between Help and Save
notes.body:
On phone/tablet layouts (<=1024px) the Eth status item is hidden
entirely, leaving the device's current IP with nowhere to show. Adds
a dedicated grid cell (status-item-brand-ip) in the help/save row,
fed by the same startHeaderDateTimePolling() poll that already drives
the desktop Eth status item.

notes.summary: fix: Test Bus Wires reliability + UI rework from real field capture
notes.body:
A timestamped serial capture (monitor_filters=time, new source-tag +
queue-depth logging) showed the requested delay is measured from
telegram-queued, not physically-sent, so 08 54/08 55's ~1.8s of hidden
TX time was eating into the intended gap - bumped TBW_CYCLE_DELAY_MS
3000->4000 to compensate. Field testing also showed a single 09 2C
doesn't always latch the motor controller out of blink mode, so Stop
Test now always sends it twice and is never disabled. Replaced the
blocking modal with two permanent page buttons (Start/Stop) plus an
inline running-status banner, since Stop Test needing repeated presses
doesn't suit a modal, and the field workflow has a real reason to
navigate elsewhere while a test keeps running in the background.

notes.summary: feat: add Test Bus Wires commissioning page (MoCo Settings)
notes.body:
Repeatedly blinks every motor controller's LEDs (08 54/08 55 + 09 2C
keep-alive, 3s cadence) so an installer can localize an IB+ bus wiring
fault by reconnecting bus segments one at a time. Own page/menu item
right after Test Zones, blocking overlay while running, boot-time 09 2C
safety net for a browser closed mid-test, full i18n incl. help content.

notes.summary: feat: RS485 Master/Slave role + sensor renaming (RS485 + Weather Forecast)
notes.body:
Adds a Master checkbox to RS485 Configuration so multiple gateways (or a
Touch BuCo/BuCo Premium) can share one SensorBus: unchecking it stops this
device from polling and switches to passively listening for VALUES replies
a real bus Master already generates, reusing the existing CRC-validating
parsers. The comm-error timeout (5000ms) was measured directly off a real
BuCo Premium's POLL cadence rather than guessed.

RS485 sensors can now be renamed on Settings -> Sensors -> Renaming, same as
ADIO/DIO and Weather Forecast sensors. The Function column shows a clean
function name (e.g. "Wind Sensor"), while Custom Name is pre-filled with a
distinguishing default ("OSB1-2 Wind Sensor", "OSB1 Temperature Sensor
Outside") built from the device/index only when more than one channel of
that kind exists. Weather Forecast sensors got the same "<source>
<function>" default naming (typeLabel dropped its verbose "(Weather
Forecast)" suffix, default name is now "WF <function>"), and the Renaming
table's first column is now labeled "Source" instead of "Pin" now that not
every row has a physical pin.

notes.summary: feat: add RS485 SensorBus (Somfy weather-station sensors) groundwork
notes.body:
Prepares firmware+UI for the modified EQSP32-CE arriving with a second
RS485 driver in place of the CAN driver. Adds a protocol layer and a
dedicated bus-poll task for Outside/Inside Sensor Boxes, animeo Compact
Sensor and Weatherstation M8/M13, a new Settings -> Sensors -> RS485
Configuration page plus a live status dashboard, wind/sun/temp/rain
sensor-picker integration across every Security/Comfort/Energy function,
an Error-watcher OR check against the existing Soliris wind monitor,
sensor logging, BACnet/KNX read-only points, and a "Time from sensor"
Date/Time option. Untestable against real hardware until the new board
arrives - every protocol assumption is flagged accordingly in code
comments and CLAUDE.md.

notes.summary: docs: Somfy SensorBus RS485 protocol notes
notes.body:
Frame format, CRC-8, command table, and per-device field layout for the
weather-station RS485 protocol, reverse-engineered from libSDN's
libSensorBus.dll and confirmed against a real animeo Compact Sensor.
Groundwork for the upcoming second-RS485-port hardware.

notes.summary: feat: add KNX/IP gateway (KNXnet/IP Routing, mirrors BACnet's points)
notes.body:
Hand-rolled KNXnet/IP Routing protocol layer (src/knx_port/) and a full
point model (src/knx_manager.cpp) exposing the same zone status/command/
position/angle + sensor + Weather Forecast points as the BACnet gateway,
re-addressed as KNX Group Addresses via a hybrid scheme: fixed per-point
sub-offset, installer-configurable per-category main/middle base (Network
Config screen 4) plus a client-side CSV group-address export for ETS
import. Multicast transport verified on real hardware.

Also bumps the default BACnet Device ID 18222 -> 18320: a real Touch BuCo
8-zone unit on the user's network already uses 18222, and two devices
sharing one BACnet Device Instance is a protocol violation.

notes.summary: feat: add Solar Heating function (UI, firmware watcher, BACnet, i18n)
notes.body:
Fills the reserved-but-inert "solarHeating" ZONE_FUNCTIONS slot and BACnet

when simultaneously bright and cold inside. Multi-select Sun (MAX)/Inside

notes.summary: fix: readable Event log action names + header clock 'undefined undefined'
notes.body:
Recognize the fixed 0x08 0x40/0x44/0x53 raw commands (Test Zones' unlock
step, Update Motor Controllers' bulk push, Reset to Auto's manual button)
by their actual byte pair and show a real name instead of raw hex, in both

The header clock polls /api/datetime-status continuously regardless of
login state; while User Management's login gate is up that returns a 401
with no date/time fields, which was written into the header verbatim as

fields present, otherwise leaves the existing "--" placeholder.

notes.summary: feat: nav cleanup + Network Config Wi-Fi screen + User Management UX fixes
notes.body:
Drop the unbuilt Touch placeholder, add Copy Properties Between Zones to
MoCo Settings, and stop showing the internal zoneId on Number of Zones.
Network Config gains a Wi-Fi Access Point screen documenting the fixed
192.168.4.1 address, fully migrated to i18n (6 languages) since the page

User Management: fix a literal "chrome.password" shown during login (bad
