notes.summary: feat: add User Management (login, roles, permissions)
notes.body:
Adds a login-gated Administrator/Service/User access system: salted
password hashing + RAM session cookies, a central AuthGuard route handler
enforcing role tiers, per-zone/area command restriction for User accounts,
email-based one-time password reset codes, and a User Management settings
page for creating/editing/deleting accounts. Off by default (userManagementEnabled=false)
so existing installs are unaffected until an Administrator turns it on.

Fixes a real freeze found during hardware testing: showing the login
overlay after a session expired mid-use (e.g. a 401 on Save) incorrectly
re-armed #boot-overlay, which nothing ever hid again outside the initial
boot chain - left "Setting up the gateway..." covering the UI forever.

Also: Name is now required and capped at 15 characters (client + server
validated) so it always fits the header's account indicator, which shows
Name only (role dropped to save space); overflow-safe truncation added
everywhere user-defined account text is displayed. Full UI + help content
for the new login screen and User Management page, translated into all 6
supported languages (en/cs/de/fr/hr/pl).

notes.summary: fix: OTA update check could crash device under low heap (w5500_tsk panic)
notes.body:
Check for updates ran its blocking WiFiClientSecure/HTTPClient call straight
on loop()'s task with no heap protection, unlike weather_manager.cpp's
Open-Meteo fetch (fixed after an identical 2026-07-15 crash). A real device
hit the same w5500_tsk stack-canary panic when the check ran during a
browser cold-load burst.

Mirrors weather_manager.cpp's pattern: the HTTPS call now runs on its own
FreeRTOS task, gated on free heap / largest free block / zero in-flight HTTP
requests before starting, with a transient floor reserved in the load-shed
guard for the fetch's duration and a bounded max-wait before failing cleanly.
Also removes the incidental BACnet UDP-drain stall the old blocking call
caused in loop().

notes.summary: docs: CLAUDE.md - document the whole BACnet/IP gateway phase
notes.body:
New "BACnet/IP gateway" section (vendored bacnet-stack + srcFilter
discipline, bacnet_port BBMD architecture + the never-hear-our-own-broadcast
gotcha, Touch BuCo EDE object numbering contract, boot-time object list +
restart rule, the 50KB skip-unused-BV heap incident, *_Name_Set strdup
gotcha, 2c write path = /api/command's exact RAM-only trio, 2d config,
test-workflow gotchas). Updated stale bits: loop()'s real tick roster,
tickZoneFunctionsEngine's incremental-sweep redesign + the coredump-proven
32-zone starvation incident behind it, Advanced Settings' gateway toggle
pair, and a new Network Config page bullet (was never documented since
Phase 1).

notes.summary: feat: BACnet stage 2d - configurable Device ID/UDP port + drop the temp UDP debug route
notes.body:
- /network.json gains bacnetDeviceId (0-4194302, default 18222) and
  bacnetPort (1-65535, default 47808): validated in /api/save-network-config,
  cached at boot by loadNetworkConfigIntoEqConfigs() regardless of ipMode,
  exposed via getBacnetDeviceId()/getBacnetPort() (same pattern as
  getConfiguredSubnetMask()). bacnet_manager.cpp now consumes these instead
  of its hardcoded stage-2a defaults.
- Network Config gains screen 3 (BACnet Device ID + UDP Port), shown only
  while Advanced Settings' Allow BACnet Gateway is on - the carousel/dots
  skip it otherwise. Values persist even while the gateway is off so
  toggling it doesn't lose them. Same Apply & Restart flow as the IP fields.
- Removed GET /api/debug/network-udp-test per its own doc comment - real
  BACnet Who-Is/I-Am traffic long since superseded the synthetic broadcast
  proof (also drops the route's eqsp32 call on the async_tcp task).

notes.summary: feat: BACnet stage 2c - WriteProperty commands + Touch BuCo EDE numbering
notes.body:
BMS writes now drive zones through the exact same path as the web UI:
- New writable per-zone command BVs (created for every zone): UP_BV(13)/
  STOP_BV(14)/DOWN_BV(15)/MY_POSITION_BV(16) are momentary (write 1 ->
  queueIbPlusCommand with control.js's own byte pairs, coalesce=true, PV
  snaps back to 0); LOCK_UNLOCK_BV(17) is stateful (08 06/08 07 + deferred
  zoneLocked sync via new requestZoneLockedSet(), PV tracks the real flag);
  ENABLE_DISABLE_SUN_PROTECTION_BV(18) mirrors the Sun page's enable
  checkbox via new requestSunProtectionEnable() (no telegram, no event).
- BLIND_POSITION_AV/BLIND_ANGLE_AV are now writable: position/angle writes
  queue a goto-pos holding the other axis at its current snapshot value;
  av.c's Min/Max enforce 0-100 % and -90..90 deg. The angle AV now serves/
  accepts plain DEGREES both ways (new decodeIbPlusAngleDeg(), the exact
  inverse of encodeIbPlusAngle()) - the raw IB+ byte never leaks to the BMS.
- Every command write mirrors a browser click downstream: same telegrams,
  requestZoneManualPending() Manual highlight, EVT_FN_MANUAL event log
  entries (explicit user decision).
- All per-zone instance offsets and object names renumbered/renamed to
  match the reference Touch BuCo EDE file exactly (241111 somfy_EDE.csv,
  committed as the numbering contract): AVs 20/21 -> 0/1, status BVs 1-11
  -> EDE offsets 0-12 with Z<n>_*_BV names (9/10 = solarHeating/
  maintainHeat stay deliberate holes).
- Status BVs are now Binary_Value_Write_Disable()'d - a BMS write gets a
  clean Write_Access_Denied instead of being silently overwritten by the
  1s refresh.
- WritePropertyMultiple registered (wpm.c + h_wpm.c added to the vendored
  lib's srcFilter) - BMS controllers commonly batch writes with it.
- zone snapshot gains zoneLocked (+ getZoneLockedFlag()) for LOCK_UNLOCK
  PV feedback; both new request*() flags are consumed by the per-zone
  sweep exactly like g_needsManualPending (no flash I/O on the BACnet
  dispatch path).

notes.summary: chore: remove temporary diagnostics (loop profiler, loop WDT, BACnet/HW/IB+/DIO debug logs)
notes.body:
All instrumentation from the BACnet loop-stall/freeze investigation has done
its job: the ~8s starvation was root-caused (zoneCount cap + incremental
sweep, both verified on 32 zones), the IB+ queue waits measured ~0ms, and the
DIO button path was proven working. Removed: main.cpp's reportSlowLoopSection
profiler + enableLoopWDT(), bip_socket.cpp's BACNET DEBUG RX/TX logs,
hardware_io.cpp's HW SAMPLE DEBUG per-pin timing, ib_plus.cpp's IB+ QUEUE
DEBUG print (+ its queuedAtMs field), zone_functions.cpp's DIO BTN DEBUG.
Permanent diagnostics (HEAP, NET, BACNET boot lines) stay.

notes.summary: fix: BACnet weather points need a restart hint + device clock UTC offset/diagnostics
notes.body:
Follow-ups from the successful 32-zone test of 1.0.97 (169 points in BDT,
UI loads fine - the heap fix holds):

- Weather points missing in BDT: the whole toggle->save->boot-read chain
  verified consistent by code reading (weather-forecast.js marks the
  'weather' scope dirty, keys match bacnet_manager.cpp's table exactly),
  and the user had enabled the metrics BEFORE the restart - yet the point
  count implies zero weather objects existed at boot, i.e. /weather.json
  was absent or all-disabled at that moment (the interleaved uploadfs
  wipes every config file; the enablement likely belonged to the pre-wipe
  state or sat unsaved). Not decidable remotely, so: (1) an explicit boot
  log line now names the condition ("No weather objects - /weather.json
  missing or no metrics enabled") instead of leaving it ambiguous against
  a code bug, and (2) the real gap either way - saving the weather scope
  never offered the header restart - is closed: performGlobalSave() now
  calls markRestartRequired() for 'weather' saves too while
  allowBacnetGateway is on (was hardware/container only), same
  boot-time-object-list rule.

- Device object Local_Time reported as nonsense: the sync mechanism reads
  correct (datetime_init() runs inside Device_Init() before the first
  timesync; struct semantics and the uint64 epoch math check out), so add
  the missing pieces and proof: UTC_Offset property is now set truthfully
  (BACnet convention = minutes WEST of UTC, CET -60/CEST -120, computed
  from localtime vs gmtime with midnight day-wrap folded in; DST stays
  baked into local time, datetime_dst_enabled stays false), and the first
  successful sync prints "Device clock synced to YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" so
  the next hardware run distinguishes "sync never ran" from "BDT dialog
  showed stale pre-sync values" (re-open the dialog in the latter case).

Requires uploadfs alongside the flash (app.js changed).

notes.summary: fix: 32-zone BACnet heap exhaustion + weather points + real Device version/clock
notes.body:
The 32-zone hardware test (1.0.96) proved the sweep works - BACnet
requests answered in 2-4ms with 32 zones configured, tick calls ~0.9s
instead of 9s - but exposed the next bottleneck: RAM. 32 zones x 13
unconditional per-zone BVs = 421 calloc'd bacnet-stack objects measured
~50KB of heap (free fell from ~105KB at 1 zone to ~56KB, minimum 3.5%),
pinning free heap near the HTTP load-shed guard's 40KB floor - every web
UI cold load got 503-shed, the auto-reload retried into the same
condition, and the UI sat on "Loading gateway configuration..." forever
(the guard correctly kept the device alive the whole time).

Fixes and additions, all in bacnet_manager.cpp:
- Zone BVs are now created ONLY for functions the zone actually uses
  (functions.<key>.state != "unused", read per zone at boot via
  readZoneFileWithLock() - the mutex exists at static-init time, and the
  tick engine isn't running yet during setup()). manual/lock/error are
  always non-unused by design; everything else opts in, so a default zone
  drops from 13 BVs to ~5. Unreadable zone file (fresh seed in flight)
  falls back to the full set - never silently fewer objects than
  configured. Enabling a function later needs the usual restart, same
  boot-time-object-list rule as every other BACnet config change.
- Weather Forecast virtual sensors (user request): /weather.json's
  enabled metrics become WEATHER_TEMPERATURE/SOLAR_RADIATION/WIND_SPEED/
  WIND_DIRECTION AIs + WEATHER_RAIN BI at instances 20+ (never colliding
  with pin-numbered 1-16), values pushed from getWeatherCachedSnapshot()
  only while its state is "ok".
- Device object polish (user report: stale-looking BDT device page):
  Application_Software_Version/Firmware_Revision now carry
  FIRMWARE_VERSION, and Local_Date/Local_Time work - bacnet-stack's
  mstimer-based clock (datetime_mstimer.c) is fed via datetime_timesync()
  from the SNTP-managed system clock (retried until the clock is set,
  then refreshed every ~60s). Note Device-18222 appearing in the object
  list is standard BACnet - every device contains its own Device object.

notes.summary: feat: spread the zone automation sweep across loop() iterations
notes.body:
tickZoneFunctionsEngine() used to process every zone in one call -
measured ~280ms of LittleFS work per zone on real hardware, so 32 zones
blocked a single loop() iteration for ~9s (coredump-proven: loopTask stuck
in LittleFS.exists() inside this engine while the BACnet gateway starved
down to one UDP drain per ~9s and DIO blind buttons were sampled just as
rarely). The zoneCount cap (1ece440) fixed the user's leftover-zoneIndex
case, but a real 32-active-zone installation still paid the full block.

The engine is now an incremental sweep state machine:
- The container/hardware config documents are loaded once per sweep into
  statics (g_sweepContainerDoc/g_sweepHwDoc) and live for the whole sweep;
  a config save mid-sweep is picked up by the next sweep (staleness
  bounded by one sweep, same as the old whole-tick snapshot semantics).
- The per-zone loop processes zones under a SWEEP_ZONE_BUDGET_MS (200ms)
  budget per call, checked BEFORE each zone (so the cheap-skip continue
  paths - notably a missing zone file's ~250ms exists() probe, the exact
  call the coredump caught - are bounded too), and resumes from
  g_sweepPos on the next loop() iteration. The ~1100-line per-zone watcher
  body is untouched - it reads the sweep statics through local aliases.
- Global gates (pin-mode warmup, container write-in-progress, parse-bad,
  HTTP save backoff, backup job via loop()'s own guard) PAUSE a sweep in
  flight rather than abandoning it.
- Sweep finalization (snapshot pruning, endLockTimerTick() family, the
  Heartbeat broadcast) runs only after the last zone, once per sweep,
  exactly like the old once-per-tick tail; sweeps are paced by
  TICK_INTERVAL_MS between one sweep's end and the next one's start.
- The hardware-pin pre-pass (blind buttons, lock contacts) is extracted
  into runHardwarePinPrePass() and runs on its own ~1s cadence even
  MID-sweep (maybeRunHardwarePinPrePass(), using the current sweep's
  documents) - button/contact reaction time no longer scales with zone
  count at all. Its lockInstant[] output moved to file scope; being
  level-based, a zone processed seconds into a sweep now sees the
  contact's current level, fresher than the old start-of-tick copy.

At a small zone count a sweep completes in one call and the pacing
degenerates to exactly the old 1s tick. The temporary loop profiler stays
in to confirm the per-call bound on hardware.

notes.summary: feat: map every configured ADIO/DIO type to BACnet + zone-independent pulse-wind sampling
notes.body:
Three user requirements from the 1.0.94 hardware test (which confirmed
rain/sun/name display all working):

1. EVERY configured pin type is now a BACnet object, not just sensors -
   the user's DIO10 alarm_input was invisible in BDT. New BIs: ALARM_INPUT,
   LOCK_ZONE, LOCK_AREA, BLIND_BUTTON_UP/DOWN, BLIND_BUTTON_AREA_UP/DOWN,
   ERROR_OUTPUT (read-only POUT state; a writable BO is stage 2c territory
   if ever wanted); new AI: INSIDE_TEMPERATURE (temp_inside). All served
   from the existing pin snapshot - SWT/POUT state reads are
   non-destructive, so no new read-ownership concerns.

2. A configured sensor must measure WITHOUT any zone binding. The pulse
   wind sensor was the violator: the PCC counter's reader was the zone
   Wind watcher's readWindSpeedKmh() call, so an unbound sensor sat at 0
   forever (BACnet, dashboards AND the sensor history log). Ownership is
   now inverted: hardware_io.cpp's new tickPccWindSampler() (always on,
   ~2s cadence, gated only on pin modes being applied) is the counter's
   ONE reader, feeding the existing km/h cache; the Wind watcher,
   sensor_logger, pin snapshot, dashboards and BACnet are all cache
   consumers. readWindSpeedKmh()'s wind_pulse_hz branch no longer touches
   the pin at all (also fixes its unconditional readPin() that fired even
   before type dispatch). Sensor history logging for pulse wind therefore
   also works unbound - sensor_logger already read this cache.

3. NTC temperature double-conversion (the second deferred sensor
   limitation, now closed): temp_outside/temp_inside with config.method
   "ntc" (the default, matching pinModeForType()'s TIN fallback) sets the
   binding's passthrough flag - the snapshot already carries CONVERT_TIN()
   Celsius, so the linear rawMin/rawMax mapping is skipped instead of
   double-converting. 0-10V/4-20mA methods keep the linear calibration.

Requires uploadfs alongside the flash (app.js comment sync).

notes.summary: feat: map wind_pulse_hz (Soliris pulse wind on DIO) to BACnet + protect PCC pins from the sampler
notes.body:
The user's real installation carries the Soliris wind sensor's pulse
output on DIO11 (wind_pulse_hz, PCC mode) - the one sensor type BACnet
deliberately skipped so far. Mapping it surfaced a latent correctness
landmine that had to be fixed first: EQSP32's PCC pulse counter CLEARS on
every readPin(), so it can only ever have one reader - the zone Wind
SAFETY watcher (readWindSpeedKmh()). tickHardwareStatusSample() read PCC
pins like any other, which was tolerable while sampling only ran during a
dashboard's 15s watched window, but the BACnet gateway now keeps the
sampler warm around the clock whenever any sensor is BACnet-mapped - a
permanent second reader silently stealing pulses from the Wind watcher
(wind readings roughly halved, threshold reactions delayed/missed).

Fix, three coordinated parts (firmware + web UI ship together):
- tickHardwareStatusSample() (hardware_io.cpp) never readPin()s a
  PCC-mode pin. The snapshot slot instead carries the Wind watcher's own
  cached km/h (getCachedWindPulseReading() - the same single-reader
  convention sensor_logger.cpp already follows), 0 until some zone's Wind
  function references the pin. readMode() moved before readPin() to make
  the PCC detection non-destructive.
- evaluateHardwarePinValue() (data/js/app.js) wind_pulse_hz case is now a
  km/h passthrough - the count/elapsed -> Hz -> Soliris-formula math moved
  out of the browser, since the snapshot no longer carries raw counts.
- bacnet_manager.cpp maps wind_pulse_hz as a WIND_SPEED AI (per-pin,
  "WIND_SPEED_DIO11", instance = pin, km/h) with a passthrough flag that
  skips the linear calibration - the snapshot value is final units.

rain_dry_contact on any DIO pin already mapped (PRECIPITATION BI) - no
change needed there. Requires uploadfs alongside the flash (app.js
changed); the browser demo's simulated wind_pulse_hz readings will need a
matching passthrough tweak next time the demo is rebuilt.

notes.summary: fix: BACnet object names - stop dangling name pointers, name sensors per pin
notes.body:
Two changes driven by the confirmed-working BBMD retest (user verified
discovery + 16 objects fast in BBMD mode, e8a90fc holds):

1. Zone BV/AV objects showed NO name in the BACnet Discovery Tool while
   the sensor AI objects showed theirs. Root cause: every basic-object
   *_Name_Set() in bacnet-stack stores the POINTER, not a copy
   (`pObject->Object_Name = new_name` in ai/bi/av/bv.c) - the zone loop
   passed stack-local snprintf buffers that dangled the moment
   buildBacnetObjectList() returned, while the AI names were string
   literals (static storage) and survived. Names are now strdup()'d once
   at boot (never freed - the objects live until reboot too).

2. Sensor objects are now one-per-configured-pin with the pin name baked
   into the object name ("WIND_SPEED_ADIO1", "OUTSIDE_TEMPERATURE_ADIO2")
   and instance number = pin number (AI-1 = ADIO1, ... BI-13 = DIO13) -
   explicit user requirement: an installation can carry several sensors of
   the same type and a BMS must tell them apart. Replaces the
   one-fixed-instance-per-type design (SUN=AI-1/WIND=AI-2/TEMP=AI-3),
   which could only expose the first sensor of each type; the four
   per-type globals collapse into one g_sensorBindings[16] array walked by
   refreshBacnetObjectValues(). Instance renumbering is fine
   pre-deployment (no persisted-format compatibility promises yet).

Also removes the BVLC debug prints (PRINT_ENABLED back to 0,
bvlc_debug_enable() call dropped) - their job ended with the BBMD
loopback fix confirmed on hardware.

notes.summary: fix: process Distribute-Broadcast-To-Network locally - BBMD-mode discovery never answered
notes.body:
BVLC debug prints (1.0.91) captured the exact failure the BACnet Discovery
Tool's BBMD mode has had all along, in one contrasting pair:
- BBMD mode (BBMD Address = device IP): "Received
  Distribute-Broadcast-To-Network" -> the relay went out (Forwarded-NPDU
  local rebroadcast, TX len=18) but NO I-Am ever followed - the device
  never answered the Who-Is wrapped inside. Discovery failed every time.
- Plain mode (no BBMD address): "Received Original-Broadcast-NPDU" ->
  "NPDU=MTU[4]" (delivered to the application) -> I-Am broadcast + a
  correct "FDT Send Forwarded-NPDU" to the still-registered client -
  device found instantly, all 16 objects enumerated fast. (This also
  proves registration/FDT/forwarding all work - the prior test's missing
  forwards were a consequence of nothing ever being answered, not an FDT
  bug.)

Root cause: h_bbmd.c's BVLC_DISTRIBUTE_BROADCAST_TO_NETWORK case relays
the message and returns offset 0 ("not an NPDU") - upstream assumes the
BBMD's own socket receives its own local Forwarded-NPDU rebroadcast back,
and the BVLC_FORWARDED_NPDU receive case then processes it locally
("prepare the message for me!"). That self-loopback exists on BSD sockets
but not on this port's WiFiUDP/W5500/lwIP stack (confirmed: our own
broadcasts never appear as RX). Fixed in src/bacnet_port/bip.c (the
vendored tree stays unmodified, per lib/bacnet-stack/NOTE.md convention):
when bvlc_handler() returns 0 for a Distribute-Broadcast-To-Network,
deliver the embedded NPDU to the local application ourselves - NPDU
starts at octet 4, BACnet source = the originating foreign device (the
UDP sender), mirroring what the Forwarded-NPDU receive case would have
done.

The BVLC debug prints stay enabled for one more hardware run to confirm
BBMD-mode discovery end-to-end; the 1.0.90 "0 of 0 objects" oddity should
be retested in the same run (likely the same missing-local-processing
mechanism seen from BDT's post-registration side).

notes.summary: chore: enable BVLC/BBMD debug prints for the BDT rediscovery investigation
notes.body:
1.0.90 test results: the zone-tick cap fully cured the loop stall (no slow
sections after boot, every BACnet request answered in single-digit ms) -
but a new, different failure surfaced. BDT's first Search found the device,
read its object-name (the one ReadProperty that arrived, answered 31-byte
ACK), then showed "0 of 0" objects with no further requests ever arriving;
four subsequent Searches never listed the device again even though the
serial log shows every Who-Is received and an Original-Broadcast I-Am sent
within 4ms each time. Meanwhile BDT kept re-registering as a Foreign
Device every ~50s (each answered with a 6-byte BVLC-Result - ACK and NAK
are the same length, indistinguishable in our TX log).

Key code-level finding: h_bbmd.c's bvlc_send_pdu() forwards an originated
broadcast (our I-Am) to every valid FDT entry as a Forwarded-NPDU - a
second TX line our bip_socket_send() logging would show. It never appears,
so either the FDT entry is invalid at send time (registration silently
NAKed? TTL decayed?) or the forward path isn't taken - not decidable from
code reading (registration add, table linking via bvlc_init(), maintenance
aging and the forward loop all read correct). PRINT_ENABLED=1 +
bvlc_debug_enable() (both TEMPORARY, same pair used successfully during
the stage-2a BBMD bring-up) make h_bbmd.c print every received BVLC
function, the handler variant (BBMD enabled/disabled), each registration,
and each FDT-forward decision - the next hardware run answers this
directly.

notes.summary: fix: cap the zone tick to zoneCount - the proven cause of the BACnet 8s starvation
notes.body:
Root cause finally proven by the 1.0.89 diagnostic build on real hardware
(2026-07-19), with two independent instruments agreeing:
- The loop profiler logged "tickZoneFunctionsEngine took 8811-16119 ms"
  on effectively EVERY 1s-gated tick.
- The loop-WDT-triggered coredump (decoded against the archived
  dist/buco-esp32-1.0.89.elf) caught loopTask inside
  tickZoneFunctionsEngine -> LittleFS.exists("/zones/51.json") ->
  vfs_littlefs_stat -> sem_take, blocked on esp_littlefs's global mutex.

Mechanism: zoneIndex deliberately keeps every zone ever created (lowering
"Number of Zones" only lowers zoneCount - number-of-zones.js preserves
configured data), and the tick processed ALL of it - 32 entries x
(exists + open + parse) at a measured ~280ms each = ~8.9s of blocked
loop() per tick, back to back. The BACnet gateway, sharing loop(), got
one UDP drain burst per ~9s: BDT requests piled into lwIP's shallow UDP
recvmbox, replies went out with long-stale invoke IDs, and BDT read ~1
object per its ~30s retry cycle. This also retroactively explains the
identical ~8s cadence across 1.0.86 (pin sampler active) and 1.0.87
(sampler provably off) - the stall was never (only) the sampler, and the
earlier fast stage-2a scans happened before the user created 32 zones.

Fix: the per-zone loop stops after the container's zoneCount entries
(position-based, mirroring buildBacnetObjectList()'s cap); entries past
the cap also aren't marked in zoneInIndex, so their stale snapshots prune
out of /api/zone-states - consistent with the UI hiding those zones
everywhere. Missing zoneCount falls back to processing the full index.

Deliberately NOT addressed here (next planned step): a full 32-ACTIVE-zone
installation still costs ~9s per tick as one monolithic loop() block -
that needs the per-zone work spread across loop() iterations (the
backup-manager one-bounded-op-per-iteration pattern), which also fixes
DIO blind-button reaction latency at high zone counts. The temporary
loop profiler + enableLoopWDT() diagnostics stay in until that lands.

notes.summary: chore: temporary loop() diagnostics for the BACnet 8s-stall + freeze investigation
notes.body:
Three hardware tests (2026-07-17..19) narrowed the BACnet slowness to
loop() stalling ~8s per iteration - BACnet UDP packets drain in bursts
separated by a near-constant ~8s gap, each request answered within
single-digit ms once drained. Critically, the ~8s cadence was identical
with the pin-status sampler active (1.0.86) AND provably inactive (1.0.87,
where the pin-name bug kept every sensor binding unconfigured and the
mark-watched gate off) - overturning the d314c13 working theory that the
16-pin sampler was the (sole) stall source. The source is something common
to both builds; prime suspects are the ~2s-gated vendor calls on loop()
(isDeviceOnline() in tickOtaManager() - its header documents an "internet
access" check - and getEthernetStatus()/ethernetIP() in the NET logger),
but the vendor lib is closed, so this build measures instead of guessing:

- reportSlowLoopSection(): every tick*() call in loop() (and the NET
  logger's vendor-call pair) is timed; any section over 750ms logs
  ">> [ LOOP DEBUG ]: <name> took <ms>" - one test run names the stall.
- enableLoopWDT(): the 1.0.88 test ended in a permanent silent freeze of
  loop() with no panic, hence no coredump (confirmed: the stored coredump's
  app SHA belongs to an older build). With loopTask on the 20s task WDT, a
  recurrence aborts into a panic whose coredump this build's archived ELF
  decodes into an exact all-tasks backtrace. Deliberately Arduino's
  enableLoopWDT(), not a bare esp_task_wdt_add(NULL) - the core only calls
  esp_task_wdt_reset() between loop() iterations when its own flag is set,
  so a bare add would reboot a healthy device every 20s.

Both marked TEMPORARY - remove once the root cause is confirmed. Known
false-trigger risk while the WDT subscription is in: a manual Email test
send blocks loop() for up to ~30s.

notes.summary: fix: BACnet sensor objects never bound - hardware.json "pin" is a name string, not an int
notes.body:
buildBacnetObjectList() (src/bacnet_manager.cpp) read io["pin"] as
`uint8_t pin = io["pin"] | 0`, assuming a plain integer 1-16. The real
schema (confirmed against hardware_io.cpp's own reader, which always uses
`const char *pin = entry["pin"]` + pinNumberFromName()) stores it as a name
string ("ADIO1", "DIO9", ...). ArduinoJson never coerces a string variant
to a numeric type, so `| 0` silently resolved to the fallback for every
single entry - every sensor binding was skipped regardless of hardware.json
content. Confirmed on real hardware (2026-07-17): boot log printed
"Object list built - 1 zone(s), sun=0 wind=0 temp=0 rain=0" despite ADIO1/
ADIO2 being configured as wind_voltage/temp_outside. Fixed by parsing the
trailing digits the same way hardware_io.cpp does, instead of duplicating
a second copy of pinNumberFromName() in this file.

Side effect worth watching on the next hardware test: hardwareStatusMarkWatched()
is gated on at least one sensor binding existing (see the prior commit) -
with this fix, that gate will now correctly evaluate true whenever
sun/wind/temp/rain are configured, so the incremental pin sampler will
actually start running (previously it silently never did, because the
gate was always false due to this bug). Watch for
">> [ HW SAMPLE DEBUG ]" lines (>100ms per pin) to confirm the sampler
itself isn't a factor once it's active.

Note: this does NOT appear to be the cause of the remaining ~1 object/
~8s-gap read pattern seen in the latest hardware test (with zoneCount
capped to 1, all 14 objects loaded correctly this time - no more permanent
stalls - but still slowly). That test had all four sensor bindings at 0
(this exact bug), so the incremental hardware sampler was never running,
yet the ~8s gaps persisted - ruling out that sampler as this particular
test's cause. Every individual BACNET DEBUG RX/TX pair logged completed in
single-digit milliseconds, proving the device itself is not the source of
the delay; the ~8s pauses are most likely either the BDT client's own
retry/pacing behavior, or occasional silent UDP receive-queue drops under
a burst (lwIP's shallow recvmbox) recovered via the client's retry timeout.
Needs an APDU-content-level Wireshark comparison (already planned against
Touch BuCo) to pin down further - not resolvable from firmware code
inspection alone.

notes.summary: feat: BACnet stage 2b zone/sensor objects + fix loop stall starving BACnet RX
notes.body:
Stage 2b of the BACnet/IP gateway: per-zone BV objects (one per real
ZONE_FUNCTION_KEYS watcher) + BLIND_POSITION/BLIND_ANGLE AVs (instance =
100*zoneOrder + offset, Touch BuCo's own numbering), and global sensor
AI/BI objects (SUN/WIND_SPEED/OUTSIDE_TEMPERATURE/PRECIPITATION) created
only for sensor types actually configured in /hardware.json. Values are
refreshed ~1s from RAM-only sources: zone_functions' state snapshot (new
getZoneFunctionState()/getZoneCurrentPositionAngle() accessors) and
hardware_io's watched-window pin snapshot (new hardwareStatusMarkWatched()/
getHardwareStatusSnapshot()). Zone objects are capped to the container's
zoneCount (not all of zoneIndex - number-of-zones.js deliberately never
truncates zoneIndex on a count reduction, so without the cap BDT kept
showing 417 objects after the user dropped to 1 zone).

Real-hardware BDT testing (2026-07-17) hit a wall: reads fast for ~30s
after boot, then ~30s per object with every object erroring. Wireshark +
serial timestamps proved the mechanism: loop() was iterating once per ~8s
(the 10s-gated HEAP print landed once per TWO BACnet RX events), because
keeping the pin sampler continuously warm for BACnet made
tickHardwareStatusSample()'s 16-pin round run every second - and each
eqsp32.readPin()/readMode() vendor round-trip measured ~250ms on this
device, so one round = 32 vendor calls = ~8s of blocked loop(). With one
bip_receive() per tick, lwIP's ~6-deep UDP recvmbox overflowed and the
device answered invoke IDs ~50s stale (ACK[77] while BDT sent [104]),
which the client discards - hence "No response" on every object. The
fast first ~30s were the pin-mode boot warmup, during which the sampler
is skipped entirely.

Fixes, all three proven against that evidence:
- tickHardwareStatusSample() is now incremental: one pin's readPin+readMode
  per loop() iteration (worst-case ~0.5s stall instead of ~8s), same
  once-per-round per-pin cadence so PCC pulse-counter semantics are
  unchanged. Temporary >100ms per-pin debug log kept for the next test.
- tickBacnetManager() drains up to 8 datagrams per tick (was 1), so a
  backlog clears immediately after any stall instead of one stale packet
  per iteration.
- hardwareStatusMarkWatched() is only called while at least one sensor
  AI/BI object exists - a config with no BACnet-mapped sensors doesn't pay
  for the sampler at all.

Temporary >> [ BACNET DEBUG ] RX/TX logs (bip_socket.cpp, with ms
timestamps and heap state) stay in until the fix is confirmed on hardware.

notes.summary: feat: add header Restart button for boot-only config changes
notes.body:
advancedSettings.allowBacnetGateway (and, once Stage 2b lands, the
BACnet object list built from zone count/hardware sensors) is only
read once at boot - toggling it in the web UI silently had no effect
without a manual restart, discovered while testing the BACnet gateway
(opening/closing a serial monitor's DTR reset was the only way it
"worked").

Adds a shared header Restart button (next to the clock, hidden unless
needed) that appears after saving a container/hardware change while
the BACnet gateway is enabled, confirms, saves anything still dirty,
restarts, and waits for the device to come back - replacing the
earlier Advanced-Settings-only version of this flow with one that'll
cover Number of Zones and hardware config too. On phones the clock
swaps for the button instead of both competing for the same header
slot; tablet/desktop show both.

notes.summary: feat: implement BACnet/IP gateway with BBMD/Foreign Device support (Phase 2, stages 2a)
notes.body:
Vendors bacnet-stack (lib/bacnet-stack/, pinned commit ddf24f7, curated
via library.json's srcFilter) and adds a minimal BACnet/IP Device object
(src/bacnet_manager.h/.cpp) answering Who-Is/I-Am and ReadProperty over
a UDP datalink bridged to the EQSP32 vendor W5500 Ethernet driver
(src/bacnet_port/). The datalink implements bacnet-stack's core
bacnet/datalink/bip.h API (not the simpler non-BBMD ESP32-port style
initially tried) specifically so the vendored, unmodified
basic/bbmd/h_bbmd.c could be wired in for BBMD/Foreign Device Table
support - real-hardware testing showed the BACnet Discovery Tool's
cross-subnet scan mode (and the reference Touch BuCo BACnet product)
depend on Register-Foreign-Device / Distribute-Broadcast-To-Network,
not just a plain broadcast Who-Is.

Also adds a "Restart Device Now" flow to Advanced Settings (new
POST /api/restart) since allowBacnetGateway is only read once at boot -
a real UX gap discovered while testing (toggling the setting silently
did nothing without a restart).

Verified end-to-end on real hardware: broadcast Who-Is/I-Am, confirmed
ReadProperty (object-list/object-name), and the BBMD-relayed discovery
workflow via Register-Foreign-Device + Distribute-Broadcast-To-Network,
all Wireshark-confirmed.

notes.summary: feat: add BACnet/KNX gateway groundwork (Advanced toggles, Network Config IP/DNS, UDP spike)
notes.body:
Phase 1 of the BACnet/IP + KNX gateway proposal: mutually-exclusive
Advanced Settings toggles (allowBacnetGateway/allowKnxGateway, both
inert placeholders so far), a new Network Config page (Settings ->
Options -> Basic Settings) for Ethernet IP/DHCP + DNS backed by
network.json and POST /api/save-network-config, and a temporary UDP
broadcast spike route to prove raw UDP transits the EQSP32 vendor
W5500 Ethernet driver - the go/no-go gate for both future gateways
(BACnet needs broadcast, KNX needs multicast). Verified end-to-end on
real hardware this session: DHCP/static IP round-trip, toggle mutual
exclusivity, and the UDP spike (Wireshark-confirmed broadcast packet
on the wire, 3/3 clean sends).

notes.summary: feat: implement Settings/Energy/Block Heat function (UI + firmware watcher)
notes.body:
Gives the reserved blockHeat priority slot a real watcher (bright + hot
gates, AND-combined, debounced) and a 10-screen config carousel, following
the Cooling/Sun/Frost-Ice templates. Fully localized (UI + help) across all
6 supported languages from day one.

notes.summary: feat: implement Settings/Security/Frost-Ice function (UI + firmware watcher)
notes.body:
Adds Frost/Ice protection as the frost/ice half of the existing
snowFrostIceRain priority slot (shared with Rain/Snow): its own
sensors, threshold, delays and priority action, with a runtime
activeTrigger field recording which sub-trigger owns an activation so
Step B applies the right action and only the owning trigger's release
ends it. Includes the 8-screen config carousel, a manual reset that
clears the Ice rain-history latch, two new priority actions
(Intermediate Position 1/2 = My Position + Lock Only), and localized
help/UI strings in all 6 languages.

notes.summary: fix: never silently stamp a default Switch Config onto a zone; log manual Energy Mode sends
notes.body:
- run-tilt-times.js: rendering the Switch Config tab used to write
  options[0] (Deadman for window products) into any zone whose
  switchConfigValue was still null, and RTT Send / Update Motor
  Controllers then pushed that never-chosen control mode to the MoCo.
  The dropdown now shows a disabled "- not set -" placeholder and only
  an explicit user selection ever sets the value; buildRttTelegrams()
  already skips the telegram while null.
- api_routes.cpp: /api/energy_mode now calls logZoneEvent(EVT_FN_MANUAL,
  EVT_ACT_ENERGY_MODE) - a manually latched Manual Priority/Comfort is
  persisted by the MoCo, so the Event log must be able to answer "who
  set this mode and when". Czech comments/log lines in the handler
  translated to English while touching it.
- CLAUDE.md: document the hardware-confirmed MoCo heartbeat-watchdog
  semantics (09 47 arm state persists in the MoCo, >180s bus silence
  drives safety-UP and swallows the first ~2-3 telegrams) - the
  verified root cause of the "first zone commands after a reflash are
  ignored" investigation; resolved by config (09 47 FF disarm), no
  code change.

notes.summary: fix: eliminate reboot loops from OOM aborts, weather-fetch heap collisions and an AsyncTCP deadlock
notes.body:
Three root causes found from decoded crash logs and an on-device core dump
(procedure now in CLAUDE.md), each fixed and re-verified on real hardware:

- /api/zone-states: replace AsyncResponseStream (whole ~17KB payload in a
  cbuf grown via throwing new[] - a failed grow under heap pressure aborted
  the whole device) with a chunked response formatted straight into the
  library's malloc'd, NULL-checked send buffer.

- Weather fetch: the ~65KB TLS transient collided with post-reboot browser
  reconnect storms and starved the W5500 driver (stack-canary panic loop).
  Now gated three ways: deferred while any HTTP request is in flight or
  heap headroom is low, a 120s post-boot warmup, and a new shed-guard
  transient-floor reservation (httpLoadShedSetTransientFloor) held for the
  fetch task's lifetime.

- Migrate to esp32async/AsyncTCP 3.4 + esp32async/ESPAsyncWebServer 3.11:
  a core dump proved the recurring task_wdt-on-async_tcp reboots were a
  deadlock in old AsyncTCP (LwIP thread blocking forever on the hardcoded
  32-entry event queue while async_tcp waited on the LwIP thread inside
  tcpip_api_call). The fork's unbounded non-blocking queue with poll
  coalescing/discard removes it structurally - the 13-parallel storm
  reproducer went from ~10 consecutive reboots to zero.

Also: save_elf.py now prunes older dist/buco-esp32-*.elf archives, keeping
only the current build's.

notes.summary: fix: validate zoneId at every entry point and shrink per-zone RAM arrays
notes.body:
Every per-zone array (~20 across 6 files) was [256]-sized purely because
that's the widest a uint8_t can hold, so indexing was always safe by
construction with zero validation anywhere - but nothing actually checked
that a zoneId sourced from persisted JSON or an HTTP body fell in the real
32..63 range. Adds isValidZoneId() (src/zone_id_bound.h) at every place a
zoneId enters from outside, then shrinks the arrays to that bound now that
it's safe to. Saves ~34.5KB RAM (129,696 -> 94,368 bytes, 39.6% -> 28.8%).

notes.summary: feat: implement Settings/Energy/Cooling function (UI + firmware watcher)
notes.body:
Adds the 9-screen Cooling config page (Settings -> Energy -> Cooling,
mirroring Sun Protection's structure) with full i18n/help content in all 6
languages, plus the zone_functions.cpp watcher: night-ventilation cooling
that activates only while it's simultaneously cool enough outside, warm
enough inside, and the differential favors cooling (three independently
hysteretic gates, ANDed together, debounced through a shared Delay Time).

notes.summary: feat: archive built firmware.elf per version for crash-log decoding
notes.body:
scripts/save_elf.py (wired via platformio.ini's extra_scripts) copies
every built firmware.elf into dist/buco-esp32-<version>.elf, keyed off
VERSION - so a crash backtrace from a device running an older version
can still be addr2line-decoded against the exact matching ELF instead
of only whatever .pio/build/ currently holds. Fails open like this
project's other extra_scripts (a copy failure only warns, never breaks
the build or the PlatformIO IDE task list). Also updates the local
Claude Code permissions allowlist accumulated from this session's
approved commands.

notes.summary: feat: add single-file browser demo of the web UI
notes.body:
Lets colleagues explore the whole app (control, all settings, logs,
backups) in any browser with no EQSP32 device: scripts/make_demo.py
bundles data/ plus a simulated backend (scripts/demo/demo_runtime.js)
into one dist/buco-demo-<version>.html, seeded from
scripts/demo/sample-config.json.

Also fixes two pre-existing UI bugs surfaced while building the demo:
- end-products.js/app.js/number-of-zones.js referenced 'bi-blinds'/
  'bi-blinds-raised', icons that don't exist in the vendored Bootstrap
  Icons set, so the two Venetian blind products (and every newly seeded
  zone) rendered no icon at all. Swapped for real icons (bi-view-stacked/
  bi-justify).
- The header error badge started polling immediately on DOMContentLoaded,
  before i18n dictionaries load, so its first paint always showed the raw
  translation key ("chrome.noError") for up to one 5s poll interval.

notes.summary: feat: add bulk Update button to the MoCo ID page
notes.body:
Pushes every recorded MoCo ID entry to the bus sequentially, per record:
Unlock first (a locked MoCo rejects setting changes, and this propagates
the Unlocked state), then one Learn telegram per assigned motor slot
(unassigned "-" slots are skipped, never Unlearned), then Switch Config
if recorded, then Lock last for Locked entries. Telegram lists are
snapshotted upfront so the "sent X of Y" counter is exact and mid-run
list edits cannot corrupt the run; Abort is checked before every single
telegram. Same sequential/abortable pattern as update-motor-controllers.js
(200ms between telegrams, areaZoneDelayMs between records), all via the
existing /api/learn_command and /api/zone_value endpoints - no firmware
change.

notes.summary: feat: include HTTP in-flight request count in the 10s heap report
notes.body:
The 2026-07-14 single-PC crash log showed 38KB free / 12.8KB largest
block ~70s after boot with supposedly one idle browser connected - the
heap report alone can't tell whether TCP send buffers of streaming
responses were pinning that memory or something else ate it. Expose the
load-shed guard's existing in-flight counter and print it alongside the
heap numbers so the next crash log answers that directly.

notes.summary: feat: add Email Notification page with automatic Error-triggered SMTP alerts
notes.body:
Adds Settings -> Options -> System Settings -> Email Notification (enable
checkbox, recipient with validation, SEND TEST EMAIL, plus an SMTP Server
tab for the outgoing relay account) and wires it so a zone's Error function
activating (a likely-dead wind sensor) automatically emails the configured
recipient once per activation. Uses mobizt/ESP Mail Client for SMTP since
STARTTLS needs a mid-stream TLS upgrade stock WiFiClientSecure can't do.

notes.summary: fix: shed HTTP load under low heap/high concurrency to stop w5500_tsk reboots
notes.body:
Two browsers cold-loading the UI at once (or one browser's parallel
connections during a hard reload) could pin enough TCP send buffers to
collapse free heap, crashing the vendor Ethernet task. A fixed cap of 6
concurrently in-flight requests (one browser's own per-origin connection
limit) plus an absolute heap floor now sheds the excess with a 503 instead
of admitting it - matched on the client by fetchWithRetry() and an
auto-reload fallback for index.html's own resources. This also tightens
the config loaders to only treat a real 404 as "first run", since a
firmware 503 must never be mistaken for a fresh device and re-seed over an
existing configuration.

notes.summary: feat: redesign mobile header into 3 rows with an Error status badge
notes.body:
Collapses the phone/tablet header from 5 stacked rows (hamburger, brand,
Eth/AP, empty-version/datetime, help/save) to 3 via CSS Grid - dropping
Eth/AP/version on that breakpoint and adding a passive Error badge (green
"No error" / red "Error active", polling GET /api/zone-states) so a phone
never has to scroll past the header just to reach page content. Also
restyles the header help icon for the dark background, forces >=16px on
mobile form fields to stop the browser's auto-zoom-on-focus (which left a
user stuck with the header scrolled out of view and no way to scroll back),
and switches the mobile main-layout height to flex-based sizing since the
header is no longer a fixed height.

fix: gzip_fs.py silently reused a stale littlefs image on repeated uploadfs

AddPreAction on the littlefs.bin target fired for `buildfs` but not for
`uploadfs` once littlefs.bin already existed on disk - uploadfs just
re-uploaded the stale .bin with no error and no [gzip_fs] log line,
regardless of how much data/ had changed or how many times it was re-run.
Confirmed against a real device via curl (bypasses all browser caching)
that several "successful" uploadfs runs kept serving pre-change content.
Fixed by running the data/ -> .pio/fs_staged restage (and deleting any
existing littlefs.bin) unconditionally at module level instead, the same
way inject_version.py's FIRMWARE_VERSION injection already does.

notes.summary: feat: implement Settings/Security/Error function
notes.body:
Adds the Error security function end-to-end: firmware watcher that
auto-activates a zone (Up/Down Priority) when its Wind-bound sensor(s)
have recorded no movement in 12h, an installation-wide Advanced Settings
override, and the Settings -> Security -> Error page. Error has no
per-zone on/off toggle - it watches every zone unconditionally and simply
never triggers for a zone with no wind sensor bound.

notes.summary: fix: gzip static assets, vendor icons locally, add cache revalidation
notes.body:
Fixes a real-hardware crash/hang when loading the UI over the Wi-Fi AP from
a phone: the external bootstrap-icons CDN link render-blocked indefinitely
(AP has no internet/DNS), and ~1.6MB of uncompressed static files pulled
over slow phone Wi-Fi collapsed free heap enough to crash the W5500
Ethernet driver. Vendors bootstrap-icons locally, gzip-stages data/ into
the littlefs image at build time (scripts/gzip_fs.py), and adds 304 cache
revalidation for the static asset trees.

notes.summary: fix: replace unreliable MoCo ID motor-count auto-detection with manual switch
notes.body:
Real-hardware testing found a genuine 4-motor MoCo ID that matched none of
the digit-pattern heuristics, so getMotorCountForMocoId() is removed
entirely - Learn Zones and Run/Tilt Times' "Send over ID" now use an
explicit 1/2/4/6 radio selector instead, also threaded through the MoCo ID
bookkeeping and its edit deep-link. Also drops the per-motor hex address
hint under the Learn Zones/Run-Tilt-Times checkboxes, confirmed confusing
for a regular installer.

notes.summary: feat: add opt-in MoCo ID bookkeeping (Save MoCo ID) with CSV import/export
notes.body:
Records which zone/switch-config/lock state was last sent to each Motor
Controller ID from Learn Zones, Switch Config and Lock Motor Controllers,
gated behind a new Advanced Settings toggle - data the reference product
this device is based on doesn't normally persist. New "MoCo ID" list page
lets an installer review/edit/delete entries and import/export them as CSV.

notes.summary: feat: add Lock Motor Controllers page in all 6 languages
notes.body:
Adds Settings/Options/MoCo Settings/Lock Motor Controllers: pick a zone,
choose Send Zone or Send ID, then Lock/Unlock. Reuses the existing
/api/zone_value endpoint (cmd1=0x09, cmd2=0x49, value=0x01/0x00) with the
same Send Zone/Send ID targeting logic as Switch Config - no firmware
change needed.

notes.summary: feat: add unified i18n translation mechanism for UI and help content
notes.body:
Replaces the old per-language-per-page hardcoded help HTML (data/help/<lang>/*.html)
with a single shared key->string dictionary system (data/i18n/<lang>/{ui,help}.json)
applied at runtime via data-i18n attributes, so switching language on the Locals page
now actually translates the UI instead of only picking which help folder to fetch, and
the same translated term can be reused across pages instead of being retranslated per
page. Migrates all existing help content (22 pages) into the new keyed format with no
wording changes, adds scripts/i18n_export.py + i18n_import.py for native-speaker review
round-trips, and scripts/i18n_check_duplicates.py to catch redundant translations.

notes.summary: fix: raise task watchdog to 20s and add fetch timeouts to stop save-triggered reboot loop
notes.body:
Growing zones 8->32 and saving crash-looped the device: EQSP32_SystemMa's
~50s vendor housekeeping wedges flash/LwIP for >5s, and AsyncTCP's
per-event watchdog subscription trips even on a plain response send caught
in that window. Raise TWDT to 20s to ride out the wedge, and give every
config-save fetch() a timeout so a reboot mid-save no longer hangs the
save chain (and the browser overlay) forever.

notes.summary: feat: Comfort Energy Mode sends Manual Priority telegram and silences energy functions
notes.body:
Comfort now sends the same 08 41 telegram as Manual Priority (the motor
controller has no separate hardware notion of Comfort). Instead, while a
zone's energyMode is "comfort", the 5 energy-category ZONE_FUNCTIONS
(Block Heat, Solar Heating, Maintain Heat, Cooling, Sun Protection) are
excluded from Step B's driver search and cannot send any telegram at all -
including the deactivate action of one that was already driving - so
Comfort fully silences them until it's deselected, at which point whatever
is still active resumes with a fresh activate send.

notes.summary: feat: add Learn Zones and Run/Tilt Times help pages in all 6 languages
notes.body:
Content is adapted from the reference procedure text to match what the
Learn Zones (3 tabs) and Run/Tilt Times (5 tabs) views actually implement.

notes.summary: feat: add Settings/Basic Settings/Heartbeat page and keep-alive broadcast
notes.body:
Adds the per-zone bus-cable-monitoring watchdog toggle (arms/disarms via
09 47, value B4/FF on change) plus a firmware-side installation-wide 08 48
broadcast sent every 60s whenever any zone has it armed. Help pages added
in all 6 supported languages.

notes.summary: fix: eliminate remaining task_wdt crashes and dead DIO inputs
notes.body:
Several confirmed real-hardware incidents this session, all stemming from
two root causes:

1. littlefs rewrites a whole file on any in-place write before its end (a
   CTZ skip-list property) - event_logger.cpp/sensor_logger.cpp's ring
   files updated a header at offset 0 on every append, turning a routine
   log write into a multi-second blocking flash rewrite that starved
   async_tcp. Replaced with two alternating append-only files per log/
   sensor; CSV/JSON exports rewritten as chunked responses since a full
   log no longer fits in RAM to buffer.

2. Any eqsp32.* vendor-library call is unsafe on the async_tcp task: the
   vendor's own EQSP32_SystemMa task can wedge for 5+ seconds, and a
   blocking call into it from an HTTP handler trips the watchdog just from
   loading a page. Moved /api/hardware-status, /api/datetime-status's
   Ethernet fields, /api/ota-status, and the sun routes onto RAM caches
   refreshed from loop()'s task instead.

Also: RS485 sends moved off loop() onto a dedicated TX task (telegrams no
longer wait on unrelated tick work); ADIO/DIO pin-mode application deferred
off async_tcp, retried with readMode() verification, and held back for a
~30s boot warmup window after real hardware showed early pinMode() calls
silently failing while late ones always succeeded; the zone automation
engine and sensor sampler now gate on pin modes being confirmed so they
don't read garbage during that window; blind-button state machines no
longer swallow the first press after boot.

notes.summary: fix: eliminate task_wdt crashes from blocking RS485 sends and Serial output
notes.body:
Two independent real-hardware crash causes, both traced through several
rounds of instrumented testing:

1. Physically sending an IB+ telegram (~900ms at 300 baud, 3x repeat) used
   to happen synchronously wherever it was triggered - directly on the
   async_tcp task for every HTTP command route, and inside
   zone_functions.cpp's per-zone loop while g_zoneFunctionsFileMutex was
   held. Under a burst of manual commands or an Area send touching several
   zones, this starved async_tcp's own watchdog (confirmed via task_wdt
   aborts with the vendor library's EQSP32_SystemMa task preempting it).
   Fixed with a single outbound queue (ib_plus.cpp's queueIbPlusCommand()/
   queueIbPlusGotoPos()/queueIbPlusZoneValue()) that every send path now
   pushes into instead of sending directly; tickIbPlusQueue() (main.cpp's
   loop()) drains one bounded telegram per iteration, off any mutex and off
   async_tcp entirely.

   Manual Control's jog-style commands (Zone/Area Control's Up/Stop/My/Down
   and Advanced Apply) opt into per-zone coalescing (a `coalesce` field on
   /api/command and /api/goto_pos) so rapid repeated clicks replace a
   still-queued older command instead of piling up FIFO behind IB+'s bus
   ceiling - confirmed on real hardware that without this, 10 rapid clicks
   queued 10 separate multi-second-stale sends. Coalescing can only ever
   overwrite another coalesce-eligible (manual) entry, never an
   automation-queued one, so automatic functions always get every telegram
   they queue. A new #command-busy-overlay gives the same visual "still
   working" cue the old synchronous response used to provide for free.

2. This board (esp32-s3-devkitm-1) has no external USB-UART bridge chip -
   Serial routes through the chip's own USB-Serial-JTAG peripheral, which
   (like native USB CDC) can block the calling task when nothing is
   actively reading it. A real capture showed a ~57s gap with zero output
   (not even the unconditional 10s heap report), and because
   sendIbPlusCommand()/sendIbPlusGotoPos()/sendIbPlusZoneValue() used to
   print before physically sending, a stuck print delayed the real bus
   transmission behind it. Reordered all three to send first, print after,
   plus a larger Serial TX buffer for extra headroom.

Also fixes Log -> Event never showing a function's "Off" transition
(On/Off is now logged on every actual driver change, not gated on the
configured action being something other than "noAction", which is the
default for most functions' deactivate side).

Temporary instrumentation left in place (marked TEMPORARY DEBUG in
ib_plus.cpp) to keep measuring real per-telegram queue wait time while a
remaining DIO-button-triggered delay report is still being chased.

notes.summary: feat: add MoCo Settings -> Switch Config page
notes.body:
Lets a specialist remap which sensor input drives which output on the
same animeo IB+ 2-/4-/6-unit Motor Controller (Send Zone or Send ID),
using cmd1=0x09/cmd2=0x18 value codes taken from real captured
telegrams. Reuses the existing generic /api/zone_value endpoint, so it
is excluded from the Event log by construction. Also hardens the Learn
Zones MoCo ID field with the same digits-only input filter.

notes.summary: feat: add Log -> Event activity log, rename Manual to Manual Control
notes.body:
Log -> Event now lists every automated and manual command sent to a zone
(icon/function/zone/action), backed by a new fixed-size ring buffer
(src/event_logger.h/.cpp) mirroring sensor_logger.cpp's file mechanics.
Covers the 7 toggle-style ZONE_FUNCTIONS entries plus Manual Control,
Energy Timer, Reset to Auto and Timer's singleEvent slot - the three
functions that deliberately bypass the priority engine and aren't in
ZONE_FUNCTIONS. Log -> Export gains a matching CSV download.

Ring-file creation is a deferred, chunked background job (one bounded
~4KB write per tick) rather than one ~192KB blocking write - an initial
one-shot version of this blocked loop() long enough to trip the task
watchdog and reboot the device on real hardware. logZoneEvent() is a
single entry point safe to call from any task (HTTP handlers only ever
enqueue in RAM, never touch flash directly).

Renamed the 'manual' ZONE_FUNCTIONS label to 'Manual Control' in the
Zone Details priority table.

notes.summary: feat: add Settings/Comfort/Sun (sun protection + sun tracking)
notes.body:
Implements the real Sun Protection automation end-to-end: an 11-screen
Settings/Comfort/Sun config UI (season, sensors, threshold, delay,
Sun ON/OFF, pre open slats, azimuth/elevation range, temperature limit)
and the matching zone_functions.cpp watcher, making the previously
reserved-but-unused ZONE_FUNCTIONS "sunProtection" entry a working
priority-engine driver like Wind/Alarm/Rain-Snow.

Consumes sun_tracking.cpp's computeSunTracking() (built earlier as
unconsumed groundwork) for the new "Sun Tracking" action, which needed
its own continuous recompute-and-resend timer since its target moves
while driving, unlike every other action. The Temperature Limit gate
is the first real consumer of sensor_logger.h's 24h-history lookup.
Adds a permanent GET /api/sun-position endpoint for the UI's live
azimuth/elevation preview, help pages in all 6 languages, and updates
CLAUDE.md's architecture notes to match.

notes.summary: feat: add Log -> Sensors history chart and Log -> Export
notes.body:
Adds a ~4-week ring-buffer history (15-min min/max) for every measuring
ADIO/DIO sensor and enabled Weather Forecast metric, a zoomable/pannable
canvas band chart to view it, and a CSV export page. Also relocates the
pin calibration helpers into hardware_io.h/.cpp so sensor_logger.cpp can
reuse them instead of duplicating them a third time, and fixes a race
where the new logger could have read a wind_pulse_hz pin's self-clearing
pulse counter out from under zone_functions.cpp's Wind watcher.

notes.summary: fix: left-align live sensor values on ADIO/DIO/Weather Status pages
notes.body:
Value cells were centered via .io-live-value/.io-state-badge, out of
line with the left-aligned Live Value header above them.

notes.summary: feat: add date/time sync benefit to Internet Connection wizard step
feat: add Save Changes step to Wizard before Load/Save
notes.body:
Adds a new Wizard step with a Save button and explanatory text
clarifying that Save persists changes to the device's flash storage
immediately, while Load/Save is for named backup copies rather than
what makes changes survive a restart.

notes.summary: feat: add Internet Connection info step and Update Motor Controllers to Wizard
notes.body:
Adds a new informational Wizard step (between Locals and Date/Time)
recommending an internet connection and listing its benefits, and inserts
the existing Update Motor Controllers page as a Wizard step right before
Load/Save.

notes.summary: feat: auto-detect default language from IP on Locals page
notes.body:
Mirrors Location page's existing IP geolocation (browser-side fetch to
ipapi.co, since the browser's own internet access is what matters -
the device's Wi-Fi AP has no internet uplink). Extracted a shared
fetchIpGeoData() helper in app.js so visiting both Location and Locals
in one session only fires one lookup; Locals maps country_code to one
of the 6 supported languages with an en fallback.

Also fixes header brand label (EQSP32 -> ESP32).

notes.summary: feat: add Weather Forecast virtual sensors from Open-Meteo
notes.body:
Fetches live weather data (sun illumination, rain, outside temperature,
wind speed/direction) for the configured location and exposes each as an
independently enable/rename-able virtual sensor, following the same
UX/config shape as the hardware ADIO/DIO sensors (Settings -> Sensors ->
Weather Forecast config page, top-level Sensors -> Weather Status live
dashboard, Renaming integration), gated by a new Advanced Settings master
checkbox. Not yet wired into zone automation - structured for that reuse
later, mirroring the sun_tracking.cpp precedent.

The actual Open-Meteo HTTPS fetch runs on its own FreeRTOS task rather
than blocking loop() - an earlier version that blocked loop() reproduced
a real-hardware task_wdt crash (EQSP32_SystemMa preempting loop() long
enough to starve async_tcp), confirmed and fixed during testing. Also
fixed a chunked-transfer-encoding response being fed unparsed into
deserializeJson() (HTTPClient::getStream() doesn't de-chunk; getString()
does).

Solar irradiance (W/m^2) is converted to an approximate Klux reading to
match a real sun sensor's unit; rain is shown as a simple detected/dry
state rather than a raw mm value.

notes.summary: feat: add sun-tracking computation module for future Sun automation
notes.body:
Computes per-zone position/tilt-angle targets from sun azimuth/elevation
(jpb10/SolarCalculator), facade orientation, and product type (venetian
slats, vertical louvers, or roller/screen), plus a temporary debug route
for hardware verification against NOAA reference values. Also prunes
stale prior-release binaries in publish_flasher.py and syncs the local
Claude Code permission allowlist.

notes.summary: feat: add My Position page for per-zone intermediate position/angle Send
notes.body:
Adds Settings -> Options -> MoCo Settings -> My Position: a 2-window
Previous/Next carousel (My Position 1 / My Position 2) letting a zone's
intermediate position (0-100%) and tilt angle be edited and immediately
sent as an IB+ telegram (0A 14 / 0A 16 via /api/zone_value), reusing the
intermediatePosition1/2 + intermediateAngle1/2 zone fields already
introduced by Update Motor Controllers (which continues to push only
Position 2 in bulk - Position 1 stays local-button-adjustable and is only
ever sent from this page's own Send button). Backfills those fields into
app.js's seedDefaultZones() so fresh devices aren't missing them, removes
the unused/duplicate myPositionPosition/myPositionAngle fields, and adds
translated help pages (en/cs/de/fr/hr/pl).

notes.summary: fix: close first-boot save race that left a dangling zoneIndex entry
notes.body:
loadSystemConfig() never awaited persistSeededConfig() before letting the
boot chain call loadHardwareConfig(), whose own first-run path fires an
unguarded hardware-config save - racing the in-flight per-zone seed saves
and reproducing the documented async_tcp/task_wdt crash through a second,
unguarded door. A zone whose seed save failed was also silently dropped
from retry tracking, letting a later unrelated container save persist a
zoneIndex entry pointing at a zone file that was never written (the tick
engine then probes it forever). Also add a full-screen overlay for the
whole boot+seed window so the UI visibly blocks user interaction, not just
silently swallowing sidebar clicks.

notes.summary: feat: add Update Motor Controllers page to push zone config to hardware
notes.body:
Sends the Run/Tilt Times parameter set, Operation Mode (Standard),
Reset to Auto, and Intermediate Position 2 telegrams for a zone, several
zones, or the whole installation, with sequential per-zone/per-telegram
progress and an Abort button. Optionally drives zones to their upper end
limit as the final step. Adds intermediatePosition1/2 + intermediateAngle1/2
zone fields (Intermediate Position 1 data prepared but never sent).

notes.summary: feat: add Reset to Auto page with manual reset and per-zone weekly timer
notes.body:
Re-enables a zone's automatic operation after a manual Energy Mode override,
sending the 08 44 telegram (one byte past Energy Mode's 0x40-0x43 family)
either on demand (with an optional Whole Installation sweep) or on a Lock
Timer-style weekly schedule, both able to re-send the zone's current
position/angle.

notes.summary: feat: add Standard Position page for per-zone position/angle and angle endlimits
notes.body:
Adds Settings -> Options -> System Settings -> Standard Position: a 2-screen
carousel editing the existing standardPositionPosition/standardPositionAngle
zone fields (already consumed by Alarm's Standard Position action) plus new
angleEndLimitMin/angleEndLimitMax fields, gated per-product the same way
Run/Tilt Times already gates its own fields. Promotes the shared
"no runtime"/tilt-angle-range helpers into app.js so both pages can use them.
Help content added in all 6 languages.

notes.summary: feat: add Configuration Wizard with a 14-screen guided commissioning flow
notes.body:
Wizard reuses existing pages (Locals, Date/Time, Location, a Test Zones
variant fixed to zone 0, ADIO/DIO config, Number of Zones, Learn Zones, End
Products, Run/Tilt Times, Load/Save) inside its own step viewport, plus a new
Copy Properties Between Zones page, with help content translated into all 6
languages. The static placeholder section is now a real loadView() fragment
so it survives navigation.

Also fixes three related races surfaced by testing the Wizard on a freshly
reflashed device: the sidebar was clickable before the initial config load
finished (letting in-memory edits get clobbered by the delayed load), the 5
bootstrap config fetches ran concurrently and could wedge async_tcp's task
watchdog on a device where all 5 files are missing at once, and the Welcome
screen's buttons (unlike the sidebar) could race the first-run zone seed and
leave a container referencing zone files never written to flash.

notes.summary: feat: add Test Zones page for motor controller wiring checks
notes.body:
Adds a 3-step manual test (priority down/up pulse + unlock) under MoCo
Settings, with a "Whole Installation" broadcast option so the same
send logic can be reused by the future Wizard install-test step.
Help content is translated into all 6 supported languages.

git checkout still refuses to switch branches when an ignored dirty file's

notes.body:
Automates push dev -> ff-only merge into main -> push main -> back to dev,
without depending on gh CLI or a PR merge (not installed in this env).

notes.summary: fix: silence LittleFS vfs_api spam, log network transitions, show real Eth IP
notes.body:
Real-hardware testing of the 1.0.37 partition rework surfaced two serial-log
problems and one real network issue, none related to the partition change
itself (verified fine):

- The web UI became transiently unreachable over the LAN/Ethernet path while
  the device stayed healthy throughout (both paths worked again afterwards).
  The EQSP32 vendor library's own Wi-Fi/Ethernet switching is the prime
  suspect - this project runs its own always-on Wi-Fi AP and has no Wi-Fi STA
  credentials, so that switching logic has nothing valid to manage. Disabled
  via EQSP32Configs::disableNetSwitching = true. A new >> [ NET ] transition
  logger (Ethernet status/IP, AP station count, gated to ~2s, prints only on
  change) makes the next occurrence attributable from the serial log instead
  of invisible.
- tickZoneFunctionsEngine() re-probed a missing /zones.json every second,
  and Arduino-ESP32's LittleFS.exists()/open() logs a vfs_api [E] line on
  every miss - 1Hz spam on any unconfigured device. Now probed once, logged
  once, and skipped until notifyZonesWriteEnd(true) creates the file.
- The browser fetches zones.json/hardware.json/lock-timer.json/timer.json/
  energy-timer.json directly as static files on every page load; a miss on
  any of them walks ESPAsyncWebServer's static-file fallback chain (plain,
  .gz, /index.html, /index.html.gz) - up to 4 vfs_api [E] lines per file.
  Silenced globally via esp_log_level_set("vfs_api", ESP_LOG_NONE) at the
  very start of setup(), since the underlying open()/exists() logging is
  vendor-layer noise this project's own code already reports clearly where
  it matters.

Also: the header's "Eth: <ip>" was hardcoded and would point at a dead
address the moment DHCP handed out a different one - it now reads the live
IP from an extended GET /api/datetime-status (already polled every 30s), and
the backup-manager boot log's slot-count line was hardcoded to 2 slots
instead of iterating BACKUP_SLOT_COUNT (3).

notes.summary: refactor: narrow Update Firmware to check-only, drop OTA partition
notes.body:
The in-app OTA installer only ever wrote the app partition, never
LittleFS, so an update touching both firmware and web UI left the
device half-updated with no way to tell. Installing a new version is
now always a full USB reflash via the public flasher site, which
updates both together - the Update Firmware page only checks for a
newer version/changelog and links out, with a reminder to back up via
Load/Save first.

Since no in-device OTA write happens anymore, partitions.csv drops the
ota_0/ota_1 dual-slot layout (only ever needed for that write path and
the vendor library's own Web Maintenance Panel) back to a single
factory app partition, sized larger (3MB) for the app's remaining
growth, with littlefs enlarged to ~4.9MB for zones/schedules/backups
headroom. Verified the vendor's own Arduino OTA/Web OTA ran fine
without an OTA-capable partition for an extended real-hardware period
previously - losing that specific vendor feature is an accepted trade
for the flash space.

notes.body:
Safety-net commit before reworking the Update Firmware page and
